counts: the number of tree castles of area `n`, the number of cells, with the height unrestricted: castles in which no two neighboring columns both have height at least 2, which is exactly when the castle graph (cells as vertices, joined when they share a side) is a tree ([[castle-graph](pages/castle-graph.md)], [[a005251-bijection](pages/a005251-bijection.md)]). Read left to right, the column heights of a tree castle are a composition of `n` (an ordered sum of positive parts) with no two neighboring parts at least 2, and every such composition is a tree castle

the number of binary strings of length `N` with no factor `010`, that is, no three consecutive symbols `0, 1, 0`. These strings are a reading of the tree castles (castles in which no two neighboring columns both have height at least 2): the gap map writes a tree castle of area `n` as a string of length `N = n − 1`, each column of height `c` becoming `c − 1` zeros and neighboring columns separated by a single `1`, and it is a bijection from the tree castles of area `n` onto these strings ([[a005251-bijection](pages/a005251-bijection.md)])

the number `W_1(N)` of binary words of length `N` with no isolated `1`, so that every run of 1s has length at least 2. `W_1` is the case `m = 1` of the words `W_m` of [[hardin-word-identity](pages/hardin-word-identity.md)] (words in `{0, …, m}^N` in which every nonzero letter is at most one of its neighbors), whose cases `m = 2, 3, 4` are Hardin's OEIS entries. The words are a reading of the tree castles (castles in which no two neighboring columns both have height at least 2): the column map sends a tree castle of area `n` to a word of length `N = n`, a column of height 1 becoming `0` and a column of height `c ≥ 2` becoming `1^c`, one-to-one and onto ([[a005251-bijection](pages/a005251-bijection.md)], [[tree-castle-by-area](pages/tree-castle-by-area.md)])

the number of compositions of `m` (ordered ways of writing `m` as a sum of positive parts) with no part equal to 2. They are a reading of the tree castles (castles in which no two neighboring columns both have height at least 2): the leading-column map puts a column of height 1 in front of a tree castle of area `n` and merges each column of height 1 followed by a column of height `j ≥ 2` into one part `1 + j`, which gives a composition of `m = n + 1` with no part 2, one-to-one and onto ([[a005251-bijection](pages/a005251-bijection.md)], [[tree-castle-by-area](pages/tree-castle-by-area.md)])

the number of skylines of width `w` with every column between 1 and 2 and tower spacing at least 2: in every row, each run of empty cells that has filled cells on both sides is at least 2 columns wide ([[tower-spacing-castles](pages/tower-spacing-castles.md)]). Such a skyline need not reach height 2, so this counts the castles of width `w` and of every height up to 2 with that spacing; the castles of height exactly 2 among them number this count minus 1, the flat row `(1, …, 1)`. The gap map followed by the complement carries the tree castles of area `w + 1` (castles in which no two neighboring columns both have height at least 2) one to one onto these skylines ([[a005251-bijection](pages/a005251-bijection.md)])
formula: the gap map, then the complement, `w = n − 1`

counts: the sum of `(−1)^{blocks}` over the towers of height at most 6 on a base of length `L` whose last column has even height, written `P_even(6, L)` (the even sector of the signed tower count), divided by `2^L`; a tower being what remains of a castle when its bottom row, which is one block, is removed: `L` columns of heights 0 to 6, all of height 0 allowed ([[signed-tower-count](pages/signed-tower-count.md)], [[tower-parity-sectors](pages/tower-parity-sectors.md)]). It is a signed sum, and it equals a count: `P_even(6, L) = 2^L W_1(L + 1)`, with `W_1(N)` the number of binary strings of length `N` with no isolated 1, so the quotient is the number of tree castles of area `L + 1` (castles with no two neighboring columns both of height at least 2), proved by a change of basis between transfer matrices ([[hardin-word-identity](pages/hardin-word-identity.md)], [[a005251-bijection](pages/a005251-bijection.md)])
formula: equal counts by a change of basis, `L = n − 1`

counts: the number of tree castles of area `n` (castles of any height in which no two neighboring columns both have height at least 2) that have an even number of blocks, a block being a maximal run of cells in one row. A tree castle of width `w` has `1 + n − w` blocks, the bottom row and one for each cell above it, so this is half the sum of `A005251(n + 2)`, all the tree castles of area `n`, and the signed Padovan number `(−1)^n A000931(n − 1)` ([[a005251-bijection](pages/a005251-bijection.md)])

the number of tree castles of area `n` (castles of any height in which no two neighboring columns both have height at least 2) that have an odd number of blocks, a block being a maximal run of cells in one row. the number of tree castles of area `n` (castles of any height in which no two neighboring columns both have height at least 2) with an even number of blocks minus the number with an odd number, a block being a maximal run of cells in one row. oeis_name: Number of base-5 (n+1)-digit numbers starting with a zero and with adjacent digits differing by one or less.

counts: the number of anchored 1-smooth strips of width `w` on the heights 1 to 6, written `strips(w, 6)`: skylines whose first column has height 1, whose neighboring columns differ in height by at most 1, and whose columns all lie between 1 and 6 ([[1-smooth-castles](pages/1-smooth-castles.md)]). A strip need not reach height 6, so this counts the anchored 1-smooth castles of width `w` and of every height up to 6; the OEIS entry reads them as three-choice paths in a corridor of height 5, starting from the lower side
oeis_name: Number of three-choice paths along a corridor of height 5, starting from the lower side.

counts: for each height `h` from 7 to 12, the number of anchored 1-smooth strips of width `w` on the heights 1 to `h`, written `strips(w, h)`: skylines whose first column has height 1, whose neighboring columns differ in height by at most 1, and whose columns all lie between 1 and `h` ([[1-smooth-castles](pages/1-smooth-castles.md)]). A strip need not reach height `h`, so each row counts the anchored 1-smooth castles of width `w` and of every height up to `h`; the terms shown are `h = 7`. Such a skyline cannot rise above height `w`, so for `w ≤ h` each row equals A005773, the count with no height limit

two sequences: the number of anchored 1-smooth castles of width `w` and height 4 with an even number of blocks, and the number with an odd number of blocks, a block being a maximal run of cells in one row. Anchored 1-smooth castles are castles whose first column has height 1 and whose neighboring columns differ in height by at most 1 ([[1-smooth-castles](pages/1-smooth-castles.md)]); for them the block count is 1 plus the number of rises from one column to the next

the number of anchored 1-smooth castles of width `w` and height 2 with an even number of blocks, a block being a maximal run of cells in one row; anchored 1-smooth castles are castles whose first column has height 1 and whose neighboring columns differ in height by at most 1 ([[1-smooth-castles](pages/1-smooth-castles.md)]). At height 2 every castle is 1-smooth, so these are the castles of height 2 whose first column has height 1, and deleting that column keeps the block count and leaves every castle of height 2 and width `w − 1`, so this is `A^e(w − 1, 2)`, the castles of height 2 and width `w − 1` with an even number of blocks
note: (deleting the first column gives all castles of height 2 and width `w − 1`)
oeis_name: Sum of every 4th entry of row n in Pascal's triangle, starting at binomial(n,2).

counts: the number of anchored 1-smooth castles of width `w` and height 2 with an odd number of blocks, a block being a maximal run of cells in one row; anchored 1-smooth castles are castles whose first column has height 1 and whose neighboring columns differ in height by at most 1 ([[1-smooth-castles](pages/1-smooth-castles.md)]). At height 2 every castle is 1-smooth, so these are the castles of height 2 whose first column has height 1, and deleting that column keeps the block count and leaves every castle of height 2 and width `w − 1`, so this is `A^o(w − 1, 2)`, the castles of height 2 and width `w − 1` with an odd number of blocks
note: (deleting the first column gives all castles of height 2 and width `w − 1`)
oeis_name: Sum of every 4th entry of row n in Pascal's triangle, starting at "n choose 0".

counts: the number of anchored 1-smooth castles of width `w` and height 2 with an even number of blocks minus the number with an odd number, a block being a maximal run of cells in one row; anchored 1-smooth castles are castles whose first column has height 1 and whose neighboring columns differ in height by at most 1 ([[1-smooth-castles](pages/1-smooth-castles.md)]). At height 2 every castle is 1-smooth, so these are the castles of height 2 whose first column has height 1, and deleting that column keeps the block count and leaves every castle of height 2 and width `w − 1`, so this is `S(w − 1, 2) = A^e(w − 1, 2) − A^o(w − 1, 2)` for the castles of height 2 and width `w − 1`
note: (deleting the first column gives all castles of height 2 and width `w − 1`)
oeis_name: Expansion of 1/((1 - 2*x + 2*x^2)*(1-x)).

counts: for each height `h` from 5 to 12, three sequences of anchored 1-smooth castles of width `w` and height `h`: the number with an even number of blocks, the number with an odd number, and the even count minus the odd count, a block being a maximal run of cells in one row. Anchored 1-smooth castles are castles whose first column has height 1 and whose neighboring columns differ in height by at most 1; the terms, the recurrence orders and the growth of the difference are tabled on the concept page ([[1-smooth-castles](pages/1-smooth-castles.md)])
note: (orders and signed growth for every `h` on the concept page)

counts: the number of 1-smooth castles of width `w` and height `h` whose first and last columns both have height 1, 1-smooth meaning that neighboring columns differ in height by at most 1 ([[1-smooth-castles](pages/1-smooth-castles.md)], [[motzkin-castles](pages/motzkin-castles.md)]). Lowering every column by 1 gives a Motzkin path of length `w − 1` and height `h − 1`, a path of up, flat and down steps from level 0 back to level 0 that never goes below it, so the counts form the triangle A097862; the terms shown are `h = 4` from `w = 7`, the smallest width `2h − 1` at which such a castle reaches height `h`
oeis_name: Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) is the number of Motzkin paths of length n and height k (n>=0, k>=0).

counts: for each height `h` from 3 to 11, the number of 1-smooth castles of width `w` and height `h` with any first column, 1-smooth meaning that neighboring columns differ in height by at most 1 ([[1-smooth-castles](pages/1-smooth-castles.md)]); the terms shown are `h = 4` from `w = 1`. Such a castle is fixed by its `w − 1` steps (up 1, flat, or down 1), and a step sequence fits in exactly one castle of height `h` when its running total spreads over at most `h − 1` levels between its highest and lowest values; in the OEIS the count is a difference of two rows of the smooth-word table
note: the difference of two rows of the smooth-word table
oeis_name: T(n,k) is the number of n X k binary arrays without the pattern 0 1 diagonally, vertically or antidiagonally.

counts: the number of 1-smooth castles of width `w` and height `h` whose last column is also within 1 of the first, as if the skyline were closed into a ring; 1-smooth means that neighboring columns differ in height by at most 1, and these are the smooth cyclic words of Knopfmacher, Mansour, Munagi and Prodinger ([[1-smooth-castles](pages/1-smooth-castles.md)]). For `w ≤ 2h − 1` the height limit removes nothing and the count is the central trinomial coefficient `A002426(w)`; the terms shown are `h = 3` from `w = 6`, where the count drops below A002426
oeis_name: Central trinomial coefficients: largest coefficient of (1 + x + x^2)^n.

counts: the number of anchored 1-smooth castles of height `h` and width `2h − 1`, castles whose first column has height 1 and whose neighboring columns differ in height by at most 1 ([[1-smooth-castles](pages/1-smooth-castles.md)]). Lowering every column by 1 gives the Motzkin prefixes of length `2h − 2` and height `h − 1`, paths of up, flat and down steps that never go below their start; `2h − 1` is the last width at which the count is a sum of four trinomial coefficients, which gives this diagonal in closed form
formula: closed form by four trinomial coefficients
oeis_name: Number of Motzkin prefixes of length 2n and height n.

counts: the number of anchored 2-smooth strips of height 4 and width `w`: skylines `(c_1, …, c_w)` with `c_1 = 1`, every `c_i` in `{1, …, 4}` and neighboring columns differing in height by at most 2 ([[m-smooth-castles](pages/m-smooth-castles.md)]). Height 4 is the diagonal `h = m + 2` for the step bound `m = 2`. A strip need not reach height 4, so this is the anchored 2-smooth castles of height 4 plus the `3^{w−1}` anchored skylines on `{1, 2, 3}`, which all obey the rule
oeis_name: a(n) is the number of subsequences of [ 1, ..., 2n ] in which each odd number has an even neighbor.

counts: the number of anchored 3-smooth strips of height 5 and width `w`: skylines `(c_1, …, c_w)` with `c_1 = 1`, every `c_i` in `{1, …, 5}` and neighboring columns differing in height by at most 3, the diagonal `h = m + 2` for `m = 3` ([[m-smooth-castles](pages/m-smooth-castles.md)]). A strip need not reach height 5, so this is the anchored 3-smooth castles of height 5 plus the `4^{w−1}` anchored skylines on `{1, …, 4}`, which all obey the rule
oeis_name: Expansion of x/(1 - 4*x - 3*x^2).

counts: the number of anchored 4-smooth strips of height 6 and width `w`: skylines `(c_1, …, c_w)` with `c_1 = 1`, every `c_i` in `{1, …, 6}` and neighboring columns differing in height by at most 4, the diagonal `h = m + 2` for `m = 4` ([[m-smooth-castles](pages/m-smooth-castles.md)]). A strip need not reach height 6, so this is the anchored 4-smooth castles of height 6 plus the `5^{w−1}` anchored skylines on `{1, …, 5}`, which all obey the rule
oeis_name: Expansion of x/(1 - 5*x - 4*x^2).

counts: the number of anchored 2-smooth castles of height 4 and width `w`: castles with first column at height 1, neighboring columns differing in height by at most 2, and some column of height 4, such as `(1, 2, 4)` and `(1, 3, 4)` at width 3 ([[m-smooth-castles](pages/m-smooth-castles.md)]). They are the anchored 2-smooth strips on `{1, …, 4}` minus those on `{1, 2, 3}`

the triangle of the anchored 2-smooth castles (first column at height 1, neighboring columns differing in height by at most 2) by width and height: row `w` lists their numbers at heights `h = 1, …, 2w − 1`, `2w − 1` being the tallest a castle can reach from height 1 in `w − 1` steps of at most 2 ([[m-smooth-castles](pages/m-smooth-castles.md)])

the number of anchored 2-smooth strips of height 5 and width `w`: skylines with `c_1 = 1`, every column in `{1, …, 5}` and neighboring columns differing in height by at most 2 ([[m-smooth-castles](pages/m-smooth-castles.md)]). A strip need not reach height 5; subtracting the strips of height 4, `A007482(w − 1)`, leaves the anchored 2-smooth castles of height 5, `0, 0, 1, 8, 46, 233, …`
oeis_name: a(n) equals the square of the n-th partial sum added to twice the n-th partial sum of the squares, divided by a(n-1), for all n>1, with a(0)=1, a(1)=3.

counts: the number of anchored 2-smooth skylines of width `w` with no ceiling: first column at height 1 and neighboring columns differing in height by at most 2, each a castle of its own height. They are the walks of `w − 1` steps in `{−2, …, 2}` that start on the floor and never go below it ([[banderier-nicodeme-2010-bounded-discrete-walks](pages/banderier-nicodeme-2010-bounded-discrete-walks.md)], [[m-smooth-castles](pages/m-smooth-castles.md)])
oeis_name: Number of sequences of n integers p(i), i=0..n-1, with 0 <= p(i) <= 2*i and |p(i) - p(i-1)| <= 2.

counts: the number of 2-smooth castles of width `w` with both end columns at height 1 and no ceiling, neighboring columns differing in height by at most 2. They are the walks of `w − 1` steps in `{−2, …, 2}` that start and end on the floor and never go below it ([[banderier-nicodeme-2010-bounded-discrete-walks](pages/banderier-nicodeme-2010-bounded-discrete-walks.md)], [[m-smooth-castles](pages/m-smooth-castles.md)])
oeis_name: a(n) is the number of paths from (0,0) to (n,0) using steps of the form (1,2),(1,1),(1,0),(1,-1) or (1,-2) and staying above the x-axis. Also, a(n) is the number of possible combinations of balls on the lawn after n turns, using a Motzkin variation of the (4,2)-case of the tennis ball problem considered by D. Merlini, R. Sprugnoli and M. C. Verri.

counts: the other counts of m-smooth castles (castles whose neighboring columns differ in height by at most `m`) tabulated on [[m-smooth-castles](pages/m-smooth-castles.md)]: the anchored ones (first column at height 1) of height `h ≥ m + 2` in the rows not listed here, each growing by width like `ρ_{h,m}`, the largest eigenvalue of the rule's band matrix; their split into castles with an even and an odd number of blocks; and the rows with a free first column and with both end columns at height 1

the number of Motzkin-path castles (castles whose neighboring columns differ in height by at most 1 and whose first and last columns have height 1, [[motzkin-castles](pages/motzkin-castles.md)]) of width `w`; lowering every column by 1 gives a Motzkin path of length `w − 1`, so they number the Motzkin number `M_{w−1}`
oeis_name: Motzkin numbers: number of ways of drawing any number of nonintersecting chords joining n (labeled) points on a circle.

counts: the number of Motzkin-path castles (neighboring columns differ in height by at most 1, first and last columns at height 1, [[motzkin-castles](pages/motzkin-castles.md)]) of width `w` with an even number of blocks; every rise is one up step, so the blocks are 1 plus the up steps and these are the Motzkin paths of length `w − 1` with an odd number of up steps
oeis_name: Number of odd Motzkin n-paths, i.e., Motzkin n-paths with an odd number of up steps.

counts: the number of Motzkin-path castles (neighboring columns differ in height by at most 1, first and last columns at height 1, [[motzkin-castles](pages/motzkin-castles.md)]) of width `w` with an odd number of blocks; every rise is one up step, so the blocks are 1 plus the up steps and these are the Motzkin paths of length `w − 1` with an even number of up steps
oeis_name: Number of Motzkin n-paths with an even number of up steps.

counts: the signed count `Σ(−1)^blocks` of the Motzkin-path castles (neighboring columns differ in height by at most 1, first and last columns at height 1, [[motzkin-castles](pages/motzkin-castles.md)]) of width `w`: the number with an even number of blocks minus the number with an odd number, which is minus the excess of the even Motzkin paths of length `w − 1` over the odd ones
note: (`A343773(n) = (−1)^n A007440(n+1)`, the reversion of the Fibonacci g.f.)
oeis_name: Excess of the number of even Motzkin n-paths (A107587) over the odd ones (A343386).

counts: the number of Motzkin-path castles (neighboring columns differ in height by at most 1, first and last columns at height 1, [[motzkin-castles](pages/motzkin-castles.md)]) of width `w` and height at most 4, so of every height from 1 to 4: the Motzkin-path strips on the heights 1 to 4, which need not reach height 4, and which lowered by 1 are the Motzkin paths of length `w − 1` and height at most 3
note: (`= (F_{2w−3} + F_w)/2`; Kociemba's comment counts these walks)
oeis_name: a(n) = (F(2*n-1) + F(n+1))/2 where F(n) is a Fibonacci number.

counts: the number of Motzkin-path castles (neighboring columns differ in height by at most 1, first and last columns at height 1, [[motzkin-castles](pages/motzkin-castles.md)]) of width `w` and height at most 5, so of every height from 1 to 5: the Motzkin-path strips on the heights 1 to 5, which need not reach height 5, and which lowered by 1 are the Motzkin paths of length `w − 1` and height at most 4
note: (its name is the same condition with heights below 6)
oeis_name: Number of (s(0), s(1), ..., s(n)) such that 0 < s(i) < 6 and |s(i) - s(i-1)| <= 1 for i = 1,2,...,n, s(0) = 1, s(n) = 1.

counts: the number of anchored 1-smooth castles of width `w` and any height, castles whose first column has height 1 and whose neighboring columns differ in height by at most 1 ([[1-smooth-castles](pages/1-smooth-castles.md)], [[motzkin-castles](pages/motzkin-castles.md)]). Lowering every column by 1 gives a Motzkin prefix of length `w − 1`, a path of up, flat and down steps that never goes below its start and may end at any level; the OEIS entry counts the same numbers as directed animals
oeis_name: Number of directed animals of size n (or directed n-ominoes in standard position).

counts: the number of castles of width `w` whose columns never drop by more than 1 from one column to the next (`c_{i+1} ≥ c_i − 1`) and whose last column has height 1, with any first column and any height; they are the Catalan numbers `C_w` ([[motzkin-castles](pages/motzkin-castles.md)], section *Relatives in the semi-perimeter grading*; [[brick-wall-castles](pages/brick-wall-castles.md)])
oeis_name: Catalan numbers: C(n) = binomial(2n,n)/(n+1) = (2n)!/(n!(n+1)!).

counts: the number of Motzkin-path castles (neighboring columns differ in height by at most 1, first and last columns at height 1, [[motzkin-castles](pages/motzkin-castles.md)]) by semi-perimeter `s`, the width plus the number of blocks, for `s = 2, 3, …`; a castle of width `w` with `u` up steps has `s = w + 1 + u`, so each up step costs one extra unit
oeis_name: Generalized Catalan Numbers x^3*A(x)^2 + (x-1)*A(x) + 1 =0.

counts: the number of castles of semi-perimeter `s`, half the length of the boundary, which equals the width plus the number of blocks (a block being a maximal run of cells in one row) whose columns never drop by more than 1 from one column to the next (`c_{i+1} ≥ c_i − 1`) and whose last column has height 1; counted by width, the same castles are the Catalan numbers ([[motzkin-castles](pages/motzkin-castles.md)], section *Relatives in the semi-perimeter grading*; [[castle-perimeter](pages/castle-perimeter.md)])
note: (peakless Motzkin paths; the mirror image without double rises is Deutsch-Elizalde's RNA-secondary-structure bijection, [[deutsch-elizalde-2016-bargraphs-cornerless-motzkin](pages/deutsch-elizalde-2016-bargraphs-cornerless-motzkin.md)])
oeis_name: Generalized Catalan numbers: a(n+1) = a(n) + Sum_{k=1..n-1} a(k)*a(n-1-k).

counts: the number of castles of semi-perimeter `s`, half the length of the boundary, which equals the width plus the number of blocks (a block being a maximal run of cells in one row) whose columns never drop by more than 1 from one column to the next (`c_{i+1} ≥ c_i − 1`), with any first and last column. Writing the column boundaries as steps gives a bijection onto the valleyless Motzkin meanders of length `s − 2`, the paths of up, flat and down steps that never go below their start, end at any height and never take an up step right after a down step ([[motzkin-castles](pages/motzkin-castles.md)], section *Castles that never drop by two: valleyless meanders*)
note: (in bijection with the valleyless Motzkin meanders of length `s − 2` of [[prodinger-2025-cornerless-motzkin-bargraphs](pages/prodinger-2025-cornerless-motzkin-bargraphs.md)]; refined by last-column height and spires on [[motzkin-castles](pages/motzkin-castles.md)])

counts: the number of anchored 1-smooth castles of any width and height, castles whose first column has height 1 and whose neighboring columns differ in height by at most 1, by semi-perimeter `s`, half the length of the boundary, which for a castle is its width plus its number of blocks, a block being a maximal run of cells in one row ([[motzkin-castles](pages/motzkin-castles.md)], [[castle-perimeter](pages/castle-perimeter.md)])

the number of 1-smooth castles of any width and height with any first and last column, 1-smooth meaning that neighboring columns differ in height by at most 1, by semi-perimeter `s`, half the length of the boundary, which for a castle is its width plus its number of blocks, a block being a maximal run of cells in one row ([[motzkin-castles](pages/motzkin-castles.md)], [[castle-perimeter](pages/castle-perimeter.md)])

the number of tower words of length `n`, the empty word included. A tower word traces, in the letters `U` (up one row), `R` (one column) and `D` (down one row), the towers left when the bottom row of a castle is removed; it is a Motzkin path with no `UD` and no `DU`, a cornerless Motzkin path. A castle of width `w` with `b` blocks gives one tower word of length `w + 2(b − 1)`, so this counts the castles by width plus twice the number of blocks above the bottom row ([[tower-word-continued-fraction](pages/tower-word-continued-fraction.md)], [[motzkin-castles](pages/motzkin-castles.md)])
oeis_name: Generalized Catalan numbers: a(n+1) = a(n) + Sum_{k=2..n-1} a(k)*a(n-1-k).

counts: the number of Dyck-path castles (castles of odd width whose neighboring columns differ in height by exactly 1 and whose first and last columns have height 1, [[castle-classification-shape](pages/castle-classification-shape.md)]) of width `w` and height at most `h`, so of every height up to `h`; lowering every column by 1 gives the Dyck paths of semilength `(w − 1)/2` and height at most `h − 1`
oeis_name: Square array read by antidiagonals of number of Catalan paths (nonnegative, starting and ending at 0, step +-1) of 2n steps with all values less than or equal to k.

counts: the number of Dyck-path castles (castles of odd width whose neighboring columns differ in height by exactly 1 and whose end columns have height 1, [[castle-classification-shape](pages/castle-classification-shape.md)]) of width `w` and height exactly `h`; lowering every column by 1 gives the Dyck paths of semilength `(w − 1)/2` and height `h − 1`
oeis_name: Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) is the number of Dyck paths of semilength n and height k (1 <= k <= n).

counts: the number of zig-zag castles of height exactly 3 and width `w`, zig-zag castles being castles whose neighboring columns differ in height by exactly 1 ([[zig-zag-castles](pages/zig-zag-castles.md)]). Writing 1 for each step up and 0 for each step down maps them one-to-one onto the 2-balanced binary strings of length `w − 1`, the strings in which every run of consecutive letters has between `−2` and `2` more 1s than 0s

the number of zig-zag castles of height exactly 4 and width `w`, zig-zag castles being castles whose neighboring columns differ in height by exactly 1 ([[zig-zag-castles](pages/zig-zag-castles.md)]). Writing 1 for each step up and 0 for each step down maps them one-to-one onto the 3-balanced binary strings of length `w − 1`, the strings in which every run of consecutive letters has between `−3` and `3` more 1s than 0s
oeis_name: Number of 3-balanced strings of length n: let d(S)= #(1)'s in S - #(0)'s, then S is k-balanced if every substring T has -k<=d(T)<=k; here k=3.

counts: the number of zig-zag castles of height exactly 5 and width `w`, zig-zag castles being castles whose neighboring columns differ in height by exactly 1 ([[zig-zag-castles](pages/zig-zag-castles.md)]). Writing 1 for each step up and 0 for each step down maps them one-to-one onto the 4-balanced binary strings of length `w − 1`, the strings in which every run of consecutive letters has between `−4` and `4` more 1s than 0s
oeis_name: Number of 4-balanced strings of length n: let d(S)= #(1)'s in S - #(0)'s, then S is k-balanced if every substring T has -k<=d(T)<=k; here k=4.

counts: the number of zig-zag castles of height exactly 6 and width `w`, zig-zag castles being castles whose neighboring columns differ in height by exactly 1 ([[zig-zag-castles](pages/zig-zag-castles.md)]). Writing 1 for each step up and 0 for each step down maps them one-to-one onto the 5-balanced binary strings of length `w − 1`, the strings in which every run of consecutive letters has between `−5` and `5` more 1s than 0s
oeis_name: Number of 5-balanced strings of length n: let d(S)= #(1)'s in S - #(0)'s, then S is k-balanced if every substring T has -k<=d(T)<=k; here k=5.

counts: the number of zig-zag castles of height exactly 3 and width `w` (castles whose neighboring columns differ in height by exactly 1, [[zig-zag-castles](pages/zig-zag-castles.md)]) that have an even number of blocks, a block being a maximal run of cells in one row. A zig-zag castle has `(c_1 + c_w + w − 1)/2` blocks, so the parity depends only on the width and the two end columns

the number of zig-zag castles of height exactly 4 and width `w` (castles whose neighboring columns differ in height by exactly 1, [[zig-zag-castles](pages/zig-zag-castles.md)]) that have an even number of blocks, a block being a maximal run of cells in one row. A zig-zag castle has `(c_1 + c_w + w − 1)/2` blocks, so the parity depends only on the width and the two end columns

the number of zig-zag castles of height exactly 5 and width `w` (castles whose neighboring columns differ in height by exactly 1, [[zig-zag-castles](pages/zig-zag-castles.md)]) that have an even number of blocks, a block being a maximal run of cells in one row. A zig-zag castle has `(c_1 + c_w + w − 1)/2` blocks, so the parity depends only on the width and the two end columns

the number of zig-zag castles of height exactly 6 and width `w` (castles whose neighboring columns differ in height by exactly 1, [[zig-zag-castles](pages/zig-zag-castles.md)]) that have an even number of blocks, a block being a maximal run of cells in one row. A zig-zag castle has `(c_1 + c_w + w − 1)/2` blocks, so the parity depends only on the width and the two end columns

the number of zig-zag strips on the heights `1, …, 5` of width `w`: skylines `(c_1, …, c_w)` with every `c_i` in `{1, …, 5}` and neighboring columns differing in height by exactly 1 ([[zig-zag-castles](pages/zig-zag-castles.md)]). A strip need not reach height 5, so this counts the zig-zag castles of every height up to 5 together; the OEIS reads the same skylines as zig-zag paths from top to bottom of a rectangle 5 cells wide, one row per column of the strip, the path's cell in row `i` being in column `c_i`; they are also the walks with `w − 1` steps on the path graph with 5 vertices
oeis_name: Number of meaningful differential operations of the n-th order on the space R^8.

counts: the number of zig-zag strips on the heights `1, …, 5` of width `w`, with first column `c_1` odd: skylines `(c_1, …, c_w)` with every `c_i` in `{1, …, 5}` and neighboring columns differing in height by exactly 1 ([[zig-zag-castles](pages/zig-zag-castles.md)]). A strip need not reach height 5, so this counts the zig-zag castles of every height up to 5 together; the OEIS reads the same skylines as zig-zag paths from top to bottom of a rectangle 5 cells wide, one row per column of the strip, the path's cell in row `i` being in column `c_i`. On the OEIS checkerboard the first column's parity fixes the color of every cell of the path, and these are the paths whose color is that of the top right corner

It is a signed sum, and it enters the castles of heights 7 and 8 through `S(w, h) = P(h−2, w) − P(h−1, w)`, the number of castles of width `w` and height `h` with an even number of blocks minus the number with an odd number; the largest root of the characteristic polynomial of its recurrence in `L` is `2ψ²`, with `ψ` the plastic number

the absolute value `|P(k, 5)|` of the signed tower count at base length 5, as a function of the tower height bound `k`: `P(k, 5)` is the sum of `(−1)^{blocks}` over the towers of height at most `k` on a base of 5 columns (a tower being what remains of a castle when its bottom row is removed, columns of heights 0 to `k`). It is not a count; `P(k, 5)` is negative at odd `k ≥ 3`, and `P(k, 5) = (−1)^k A_5(k) + B_5(k)` with `A_5(k) = k(k + 1)²(k + 2)/3` and `B_5(k) = (k + 1)²` ([[signed-tower-k-direction](pages/signed-tower-k-direction.md)], [[castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk](pages/castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk.md)])

oeis_name: Hexagonal numbers: a(n) = n*(2*n-1).

counts: `A^e(3, h)`, the number of castles of width 3 and height `h` with an even number of blocks (a block being a maximal run of cells in one row), as a function of the height; the values at even and odd heights follow two quadratics, `10m² − 5m + 1` at `h = 2m` and `m(2m + 1)` at `h = 2m + 1`, so the sequence interleaves them ([[sum-of-three-cubes-castles](pages/sum-of-three-cubes-castles.md)])

`A^o(3, h)`, the number of castles of width 3 and height `h` with an odd number of blocks (a block being a maximal run of cells in one row), as a function of the height; the values at odd and even heights follow two quadratics, `10n² + 5n + 1` at `h = 2n + 1` and `m(2m − 1)` at `h = 2m`, so the sequence interleaves them ([[sum-of-three-cubes-castles](pages/sum-of-three-cubes-castles.md)])

`A^e(4, h)`, the number of castles of width 4 and height `h` with an even number of blocks (a block being a maximal run of cells in one row), as a function of the height; the values at even and at odd heights follow two different cubic polynomials in `h`

the number of convex castles of width `w` and height 3: castles whose column heights rise weakly to the top and then fall weakly, a unimodal skyline, which are exactly the castles of height 3 with the fewest possible blocks, 3 ([[convex-castle](pages/convex-castle.md)])
oeis_name: Binomial coefficient binomial(n,4) = n*(n-1)*(n-2)*(n-3)/24.

counts: `A^e(w, 2)`, the number of castles of width `w` and height 2 with an even number of blocks (a block being a maximal run of cells in one row); the height-2 columns form a binary string, and the castle has one block more than the string has runs of 1s ([[hyperbolic-sequence-family](pages/hyperbolic-sequence-family.md)])
oeis_name: Sum of every 4th entry of row n in Pascal's triangle, starting at binomial(n,2).

counts: `A^o(w, 2)`, the number of castles of width `w` and height 2 with an odd number of blocks (a block being a maximal run of cells in one row); the height-2 columns form a binary string, and the castle has one block more than the string has runs of 1s ([[hyperbolic-sequence-family](pages/hyperbolic-sequence-family.md)])
oeis_name: Sum of every 4th entry of row n in Pascal's triangle, starting at "n choose 0".

counts: `S(w, 2) = A^e(w, 2) − A^o(w, 2)`, the number of castles of width `w` and height 2 with an even number of blocks (a block being a maximal run of cells in one row) minus the number with an odd number; a signed difference, equal to `1 − P(1, w)` with `P` the signed tower count ([[signed-tower-count](pages/signed-tower-count.md)])
oeis_name: Expansion of 1/((1 - 2*x + 2*x^2)*(1-x)).

counts: the number of castles of width 2, any height, with `b + 1` blocks (a block being a maximal run of cells in one row); removing the bottom row, which is one block, leaves the towers on a base of 2 columns with `b` blocks ([[tower-heap](pages/tower-heap.md)])
oeis_name: The odd numbers: a(n) = 2*n + 1.

counts: the number of castles of width 3, any height, with `b + 1` blocks (a block being a maximal run of cells in one row); removing the bottom row, which is one block, leaves the towers on a base of 3 columns with `b` blocks ([[tower-heap](pages/tower-heap.md)])
oeis_name: Centered pentagonal numbers: (5n^2+5n+2)/2; crystal ball sequence for 3.3.3.4.4. planar net.

counts: the number of castles of width 4, any height, with `b + 1` blocks (a block being a maximal run of cells in one row); removing the bottom row, which is one block, leaves the towers on a base of 4 columns with `b` blocks ([[tower-heap](pages/tower-heap.md)])

the number of castles of width 5, any height, with `b + 1` blocks (a block being a maximal run of cells in one row); removing the bottom row, which is one block, leaves the towers on a base of 5 columns with `b` blocks ([[tower-heap](pages/tower-heap.md)])

the number of castles of width 6, any height, with `b + 1` blocks (a block being a maximal run of cells in one row); removing the bottom row, which is one block, leaves the towers on a base of 6 columns with `b` blocks ([[tower-heap](pages/tower-heap.md)])

the number of castles of width 7, any height, with `b + 1` blocks (a block being a maximal run of cells in one row); removing the bottom row, which is one block, leaves the towers on a base of 7 columns with `b` blocks ([[tower-heap](pages/tower-heap.md)])

the number `T_3(w)` of tree skylines of width `w` and height at most 3: skylines `(c_1, …, c_w)` with every `c_i` in `{1, 2, 3}` in which no two neighboring columns both have height at least 2 ([[castle-graph](pages/castle-graph.md)]). A tree skyline need not reach height 3, so this counts the tree castles of every height up to 3 together, and the tree castles of height exactly 3 number `T_3(w) − T_2(w)`; these are the Jacobsthal numbers
oeis_name: Jacobsthal sequence (or Jacobsthal numbers): a(n) = a(n-1) + 2*a(n-2), with a(0) = 0, a(1) = 1; also a(n) = nearest integer to 2^n/3.

counts: the number `T_4(w)` of tree skylines of width `w` and height at most 4: skylines `(c_1, …, c_w)` with every `c_i` in `{1, 2, 3, 4}` in which no two neighboring columns both have height at least 2 ([[castle-graph](pages/castle-graph.md)]). A tree skyline need not reach height 4, so this counts the tree castles of every height up to 4 together, and the tree castles of height exactly 4 number `T_4(w) − T_3(w)`

the number `T_5(w)` of tree skylines of width `w` and height at most 5: skylines `(c_1, …, c_w)` with every `c_i` in `{1, 2, 3, 4, 5}` in which no two neighboring columns both have height at least 2 ([[castle-graph](pages/castle-graph.md)]). A tree skyline need not reach height 5, so this counts the tree castles of every height up to 5 together, and the tree castles of height exactly 5 number `T_5(w) − T_4(w)`

the number of Fibonacci castles of width `w`: castles of height 2 with no two neighboring columns of height 2 ([[fibonacci-castle](pages/fibonacci-castle.md)]). They are the tree castles of height exactly 2, the castles of height 2 whose castle graph (cells as vertices, joined when they share a side) is a tree ([[castle-graph](pages/castle-graph.md)]), and they number `F_{w+2} − 1`, one less than the skylines on `{1, 2}` with no two neighboring 2s
oeis_name: a(n) = Fibonacci(n) - 1.

counts: the number of castles of semi-perimeter `s`, half the length of the boundary, which equals the width plus the number of blocks (a block being a maximal run of cells in one row), of any width and height; every castle is a bargraph, so these are the bargraphs counted by semi-perimeter ([[castle-perimeter](pages/castle-perimeter.md)])
oeis_name: Expansion of (1 + x^2 - sqrt( 1 - 4*x + 2*x^2 + x^4)) / (2*x) in powers of x.

counts: the number of castles of semi-perimeter `s`, half the length of the boundary, which equals the width plus the number of blocks (a block being a maximal run of cells in one row) and width `w`, as a triangle read by rows, one row for each `s` with `w = 1, …, s − 1` ([[castle-perimeter](pages/castle-perimeter.md)])
oeis_name: Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) is the number of bargraphs of semiperimeter n having width k (n>=2, k>=1).

counts: the number of castles of semi-perimeter `s`, half the length of the boundary, which equals the width plus the number of blocks (a block being a maximal run of cells in one row) that have an even number of blocks; with `B` the generating function of all castles by semi-perimeter and `B_s` that of the number with an even number of blocks minus the number with an odd number, their generating function is `(B + B_s)/2` ([[castle-perimeter](pages/castle-perimeter.md)], section *The parity split*)

the number of castles of semi-perimeter `s`, half the length of the boundary, which equals the width plus the number of blocks (a block being a maximal run of cells in one row) with an even number of blocks minus the number with an odd number, the sum of `(−1)^{blocks}` over the castles of semi-perimeter `s`; a signed difference ([[castle-perimeter](pages/castle-perimeter.md)], section *The parity split*)
growth: `τ` (a complex pair of singularities of modulus `1/τ`)

counts: the number of convex castles of semi-perimeter `s`, of any width and height, the semi-perimeter `s` being half the length of the boundary, which is the width plus the number of blocks ([[castle-perimeter](pages/castle-perimeter.md)]); a convex castle is a castle whose skyline rises weakly to its tallest column and then falls weakly ([[convex-castle](pages/convex-castle.md)]). A convex castle of height `h` has exactly `h` blocks, so `s = w + h` and the count is the sum of `C(2h + w − 3, w − 1)` over `w + h = s`, the Fibonacci number `F_{2s−3}`; these are the stack polyominoes that Delest and Viennot count by perimeter
note: (Delest-Viennot's stacks by perimeter); `F_{2s−3}`, the anti-diagonal sums of `C(2h + w − 3, w − 1)`

counts: the number of convex castles of semi-perimeter `s` that have an even number of blocks, the semi-perimeter `s` being half the length of the boundary, which is the width plus the number of blocks ([[castle-perimeter](pages/castle-perimeter.md)]); a convex castle is a castle whose skyline rises weakly to its tallest column and then falls weakly ([[convex-castle](pages/convex-castle.md)]). A convex castle of height `h` has exactly `h` blocks, so these are the convex castles of even height

the number of convex castles of semi-perimeter `s` with an even number of blocks minus the number with an odd number of blocks, the semi-perimeter `s` being half the length of the boundary, which is the width plus the number of blocks ([[castle-perimeter](pages/castle-perimeter.md)]); a convex castle is a castle whose skyline rises weakly to its tallest column and then falls weakly ([[convex-castle](pages/convex-castle.md)]). It is a signed difference, and it repeats `−1, 0, 1, 1, 0, −1` with period 6

the number of palindromic castles of semi-perimeter `s`, half the length of the boundary, which for a castle is its width plus its number of blocks ([[castle-perimeter](pages/castle-perimeter.md)]): castles of any height with `c_i = c_{w+1−i}`, the same read from either end ([[castle-classification-shape](pages/castle-classification-shape.md)]), which Deutsch and Elizalde call symmetric bargraphs
oeis_name: Number of symmetric bargraphs having semiperimeter n (n>=2).

counts: the number of castles of height 5 and semi-perimeter `s`, half the length of the boundary, which equals the width plus the number of blocks (a block being a maximal run of cells in one row) in which no column of height 1 stands next to a column of height 2 and no column of height 4 next to one of height 5. This neighbor rule is one of 601 at height 5 whose castles grow like the silver ratio `1 + √2` by semi-perimeter, and no rule of lower height does ([[semi-perimeter-growth-census](pages/semi-perimeter-growth-census.md)])
formula: rational, denominator `(1 − x)²(1 + x²)(1 − 2x − x²)(1 − x + x² + x³)`

counts: the number of prime castles of semi-perimeter `s`: castles with no column of height 1 ([[prime-castles](pages/prime-castles.md)]), graded by `s`, half the length of the boundary, which for a castle is its width plus its number of blocks ([[castle-perimeter](pages/castle-perimeter.md)]). Removing the bottom row of a prime castle leaves a castle with the same width and one block fewer, and every castle arises once this way, so for `s ≥ 3` these are the castles of semi-perimeter `s − 1`, `A082582(s − 1)` (the row-deletion bijection, [[deutsch-elizalde-2016-bargraphs-cornerless-motzkin](pages/deutsch-elizalde-2016-bargraphs-cornerless-motzkin.md)] §3.9)
oeis_name: Expansion of (1 + x^2 - sqrt( 1 - 4*x + 2*x^2 + x^4)) / (2*x) in powers of x.

counts: the number of castles of height 2 and semi-perimeter `s`, half the length of the boundary, which equals the width plus the number of blocks (a block being a maximal run of cells in one row); removing the bottom row and lengthening each run of height-2 columns by one column gives the nonzero binary strings of length `s − 1` whose runs of 1s all have length at least 2 ([[golden-silver-bronze-plastic-castles](pages/golden-silver-bronze-plastic-castles.md)])
oeis_name: Expansion of 1/((1-2*x+x^2-x^3)*(1-x)).

counts: the number of castles of height 3 and semi-perimeter `s`, half the length of the boundary, which equals the width plus the number of blocks (a block being a maximal run of cells in one row) whose columns all have height 1 or 3; removing the bottom row and lengthening each run of height-3 columns by two columns gives the nonzero binary strings of length `s − 1` whose runs of 1s all have length at least 3, and the counts grow like the golden ratio `φ` by semi-perimeter ([[golden-silver-bronze-plastic-castles](pages/golden-silver-bronze-plastic-castles.md)])
oeis_name: Number of different possible rows (or columns) in an n X n crossword puzzle.

counts: the number of castles of semi-perimeter `s`, half the length of the boundary, which equals the width plus the number of blocks (a block being a maximal run of cells in one row) with `k` peaks, a peak (here a bargraph peak) being a maximal run of equal columns higher than both neighbors, as a triangle read by rows, one row for each `s` ([[deutsch-elizalde-2017-bargraphs-dyck-paths](pages/deutsch-elizalde-2017-bargraphs-dyck-paths.md)], [[castle-perimeter](pages/castle-perimeter.md)])
note: (the sums along `s − k = m` are the Catalan numbers `C_m`, Deutsch-Elizalde 2017)
oeis_name: Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) is the number of bargraphs of semiperimeter n having k peaks (n >= 2, k >= 1).

counts: the number of prime castles of area `n`, the number of cells: castles with no column of height 1 ([[prime-castles](pages/prime-castles.md)]). Read as compositions of `n`, they are the compositions into parts at least 2, which number the Fibonacci number `F_{n−1}`. They are prime for gluing: castles that begin and end with a column of height 1, glued at a shared column of height 1, factor uniquely into padded prime castles `(1, X, 1)`
oeis_name: Fibonacci numbers: F(n) = F(n-1) + F(n-2) with F(0) = 0 and F(1) = 1.

counts: the number `U(n)` of prime convex castles of area `n`: convex castles (columns rise weakly to a maximum and then fall weakly) with no column of height 1, which are the weakly unimodal compositions of `n` into parts at least 2 ([[prime-convex-castles](pages/prime-convex-castles.md)]). Removing the runs of height-1 columns at the two ends of a convex castle leaves its prime part, so `U(n)` is the second difference of `A001523`, the convex castles by area; the generating function is `Σ_k q^k/((1−q^k)(q²;q)_{k−2}²)`

the number of prime castles of area `n` (castles with no column of height 1) that are not convex, so that their columns do not rise weakly to one maximum and then fall weakly: `F_{n−1} − U(n)`, all the prime castles of area `n` minus the prime convex ones ([[prime-convex-castles](pages/prime-convex-castles.md)]). The first is `(3, 2, 3)`, at area 8

the triangle of the number `U(n, w)` of prime convex castles (convex castles with no column of height 1) of area `n` and width `w`, read by rows `n = 2, 3, …` with `w = 1, 2, …` in each row. Removing the bottom row matches them with the convex castles of area `n − w` and width `w` ([[prime-convex-castles](pages/prime-convex-castles.md)])
formula: convex castles of area `n − w`, width `w`

counts: the number of convex castles of area `n` (columns rise weakly to a maximum and then fall weakly) whose first column does not have height 1, `A001523(n) − A001523(n − 1)`: putting a column of height 1 in front of a convex castle of area `n − 1` gives exactly the convex castles of area `n` that begin at height 1 ([[prime-convex-castles](pages/prime-convex-castles.md)]). The OEIS entry counts the compositions whose alternating parts weakly decrease; the match is checked for `n ≤ 1001` against the two b-files
note: (`= A001523(n) − A001523(n−1)`, checked for `n ≤ 1001` against the two b-files)
oeis_name: Number of compositions with alternating parts weakly decreasing (or weakly increasing).

counts: the number of castles of area `n` counted up to rearranging their prime factors. Padding a castle `C` to `(1, C, 1)` and cutting it at every inner column of height 1 gives its prime factors `(1, X, 1)`, with `X` empty or a castle with no column of height 1, and two castles count once when one is the other's factors in another order ([[signed-prime-castles](pages/signed-prime-castles.md)], [[prime-castles](pages/prime-castles.md)]). The count is the Euler transform of the prime counts, `Σ_n a(n) q^{n+1} = Π_j (1−q^j)^{−π_j} − 1`, with `π_j` the number of prime castles of area `j − 1` and `π_1 = 1`
formula: `Σ_n a(n) q^{n+1} = Π_j (1−q^j)^{−π_j} − 1`, with `π_j` the number of prime castles of area `j − 1` and `π_1 = 1`

counts: the numbers of prime castles of area `n` (castles with no column of height 1) with an even and with an odd number of blocks, a block being a maximal run of cells in one row, tabulated on [[prime-castles](pages/prime-castles.md)], and the same split for the prime convex castles on [[prime-convex-castles](pages/prime-convex-castles.md)], where a castle of height `h` has `h` blocks, so the split is by the parity of the height

the number of castles of area `n` (`n` cells, any height) with an even number of blocks minus the number with an odd number, a block being a maximal run of cells in one row. The terms come from the row-raising recursion, a functional equation that rests on a prime castle (no column of height 1) being a castle with a full row slid under it, and they grow like `C⋆(−ρ)^n` ([[castle-row-raising-equation](pages/castle-row-raising-equation.md)])

two real constants: the growth constant `ρ` and the prefactor `C⋆` of the number of castles of area `n` with an even number of blocks minus the number with an odd number, which is asymptotic to `C⋆(−ρ)^n`. The pole `−1/ρ` of the signed generating function lies where `q E(q, q) = 1`, and it is the first zero of the q-series `M(q)` of [[castle-q-bessel-closed-form](pages/castle-q-bessel-closed-form.md)]; `C⋆` is the residue there
formula: pole at `q E(q, q) = 1`, the first zero of `M(q)` on [[castle-q-bessel-closed-form](pages/castle-q-bessel-closed-form.md)]

counts: a real constant: `q_1`, the second zero of the q-series `M(q)` whose first zero `q_0 = −1/ρ` sets the growth of the number of castles of area `n` with an even number of blocks minus the number with an odd number. Since `|q_0/q_1| = 0.7508…`, the approximation `C⋆(−ρ)^n` of that signed count has relative error `O(0.7508^n)` ([[castle-q-bessel-closed-form](pages/castle-q-bessel-closed-form.md)])

the number of castles of area `n` with `k` peaks, a peak being a maximal run of neighboring columns of height at least 2 ([[castle-foata-transform](pages/castle-foata-transform.md)]), as a triangle with rows `n = 1, 2, …` and `k = 0, 1, …` in each row. The peaks of a castle are its prime factors other than the trivial `(1, 1)`, and with `q` marking area and `t` peaks the generating function, the empty castle included, is `(1−q−q²+tq²)/(1−2q+q³−tq³)` ([[castle-row-raising-equation](pages/castle-row-raising-equation.md)])

the number of one-peak castles of area `n`: the castles `(1^a, X, 1^b)` with `a, b ≥ 0` and `X` a nonempty castle with no column of height 1, so that the columns of height at least 2 form one unbroken run
oeis_name: Apply partial sum operator twice to Fibonacci numbers.

counts: the number of monotone castles of area `n`, the number of cells: castles whose skyline is weakly increasing or weakly decreasing. Reading the column heights in order makes a castle of area `n` a composition of `n`; the weakly decreasing and the weakly increasing ones each correspond to the partitions of `n`, and the constant ones, one per divisor of `n`, are both, so there are `2p(n) − d(n)`. The OEIS entry defines its sequence by Lyndon factorizations and proves that these are the weakly monotone compositions, so `a(n) = 2A000041(n) − A000005(n)` ([[castle-add-a-column-equation](pages/castle-add-a-column-equation.md)])
note: (defined by Lyndon factorizations; the entry proves that these are the weakly monotone compositions, so `a(n) = 2A000041(n) − A000005(n)`)
oeis_name: Number of compositions of n with uniform Lyndon factorization and uniform co-Lyndon factorization.

counts: the number of castles of area `n`, the number of cells, that are not monotone: the compositions of `n` (column heights in order) that are neither weakly increasing nor weakly decreasing, `2^{n−1} − 2p(n) + d(n)` ([[castle-add-a-column-equation](pages/castle-add-a-column-equation.md)])
note: (compositions neither weakly increasing nor weakly decreasing)
oeis_name: Number of compositions of n that are neither weakly increasing nor weakly decreasing.

counts: the number of monotone castles of area `n` (skyline weakly increasing or weakly decreasing, area the number of cells) with an even number of blocks minus the number with an odd number, `2(−1)^n A000700(n) − Σ_{d|n} (−1)^d`, with `A000700(n)` the partitions of `n` into distinct odd parts ([[castle-add-a-column-equation](pages/castle-add-a-column-equation.md)])

the number of convex castles of area `n`, the number of cells, of any width and height; a convex castle is a castle whose skyline rises weakly to its tallest column and then falls weakly ([[convex-castle](pages/convex-castle.md)]). Reading the column heights left to right makes a castle of area `n` a composition of `n`, so these are the weakly unimodal compositions of `n` ([[weakly-unimodal-composition](pages/weakly-unimodal-composition.md)]), the stacks of polyomino theory
oeis_name: Number of stacks, or planar partitions of n; also number of weakly unimodal compositions of n.

counts: the number of castles of area `n`, the number of cells, of every width and height; read left to right, the column heights of a castle of area `n` form a composition of `n`, every composition is one castle, so there are `2^{n−1}` ([[castle-by-area](pages/castle-by-area.md)])
oeis_name: Coefficients of expansion of (1-x)/(1-2*x) in powers of x.

counts: the number of non-convex castles of area `n`, the number of cells: castles whose skyline does not rise weakly and then fall weakly. Reading the column heights in order makes a castle of area `n` a composition of `n`, and the convex ones are the weakly unimodal compositions, so this is `2^{n−1} − A001523(n)`, the compositions of `n` that cannot be viewed as stacks ([[castle-by-area](pages/castle-by-area.md)])
oeis_name: The number of compositions of n which cannot be viewed as stacks.

counts: the number of vee castles of area `n`, the number of cells, of any width and height; a vee castle is a castle whose skyline falls weakly to its lowest column and then rises weakly ([[castle-by-area](pages/castle-by-area.md)]). Reading the column heights left to right makes a castle of area `n` a composition of `n`, so these are the compositions of `n` whose negation is unimodal
oeis_name: Number of compositions of n whose negation is unimodal.

counts: the number of castles of area `n`, the number of cells, of any width and height, that are not vee castles; a vee castle is a castle whose skyline falls weakly to its lowest column and then rises weakly ([[castle-by-area](pages/castle-by-area.md)]). As compositions of `n` these are the compositions whose negation is not unimodal, `2^{n−1} − A332578(n)` of them
oeis_name: Number of compositions of n whose negation is not unimodal.

counts: the number of Euler castles (castles whose columns fall by 0 or 1 at each step and end at height 1, such as `(3, 3, 2, 1, 1)`, [[euler-castles](pages/euler-castles.md)]) of area `n`, the number of cells. The rows of an Euler castle are a partition of its area into distinct parts, so these are the partitions of `n` into distinct parts
oeis_name: Expansion of Product_{m >= 1} (1 + x^m); number of partitions of n into distinct parts; number of partitions of n into odd parts.

counts: the number of Euler castles (castles whose columns fall by 0 or 1 at each step and end at height 1, such as `(3, 3, 2, 1, 1)`, [[euler-castles](pages/euler-castles.md)]) of area `n` with an even number of blocks, a block being a maximal run of cells in one row. An Euler castle has one block per row, so these are the partitions of `n` into an even number of distinct parts
oeis_name: Number of partitions of n into distinct parts such that number of parts is even.

counts: the number of Euler castles (castles whose columns fall by 0 or 1 at each step and end at height 1, such as `(3, 3, 2, 1, 1)`, [[euler-castles](pages/euler-castles.md)]) of area `n` with an odd number of blocks, a block being a maximal run of cells in one row. An Euler castle has one block per row, so these are the partitions of `n` into an odd number of distinct parts
oeis_name: Number of partitions of n into distinct parts such that number of parts is odd.

counts: the number of Euler castles (castles whose columns fall by 0 or 1 at each step and end at height 1, such as `(3, 3, 2, 1, 1)`, [[euler-castles](pages/euler-castles.md)]) of area `n` with an even number of blocks minus the number with an odd number, a block being a maximal run of cells in one row (one per row on an Euler castle). By Euler's pentagonal number theorem this difference is nonzero only at the generalized pentagonal areas, where Franklin's move on the castles leaves one castle unmatched
note: (Euler's pentagonal number theorem; Franklin's move on the castles)
oeis_name: From Euler's Pentagonal Theorem: coefficient of q^n in Product_{m>=1} (1 - q^m).

counts: the number of Euler castles (castles whose columns fall by 0 or 1 at each step and end at height 1, such as `(3, 3, 2, 1, 1)`, [[euler-castles](pages/euler-castles.md)]) of semi-perimeter `s`, half the length of the boundary, which is the width plus the number of blocks and so `w + h` on an Euler castle
oeis_name: Fibonacci numbers: F(n) = F(n-1) + F(n-2) with F(0) = 0 and F(1) = 1.

counts: the number of Euler castles (castles whose columns fall by 0 or 1 at each step and end at height 1, such as `(3, 3, 2, 1, 1)`, [[euler-castles](pages/euler-castles.md)]) of semi-perimeter `s` (half the length of the boundary, here `w + h`) with an even number of blocks minus the number with an odd number, a block being a maximal run of cells in one row; it repeats with period 6
oeis_name: Inverse of 6th cyclotomic polynomial. A period 6 sequence.

counts: the number of totient strips on the heights 1, 2, 3 of width `w`: skylines with every `c_i` in `{1, 2, 3}` whose neighboring columns have coprime heights, which allows every pair of neighbors except two 2s or two 3s side by side ([[totient-castles](pages/totient-castles.md)]). the rows `A^o(·, h)` for the heights `h = 3` to 7, the terms shown being `h = 3`: `A^o(w, h)` is the number of castles of width `w` and height `h` with an odd number of blocks, a block being a maximal run of cells in one row [[odd-castles-and-block-tables](pages/odd-castles-and-block-tables.md)]. In the formula, `A` is the number of all castles of width `w` and height `h`, and `P(k, L)` is the number of towers (castles minus their bottom row) of height at most `k` on a base of length `L` with an even number of blocks minus the number with an odd number [[signed-tower-count](pages/signed-tower-count.md)]; the orders are those of the linear recurrences of the rows `h = 3, …, 7`

the columns at fixed width of the castles split by block parity, as functions of the height `h`: `A^o(w, h)` for widths 4, 5 and 6, the number of castles of width `w` and height `h` with an odd number of blocks (a block being a maximal run of cells in one row), and `A^e(5, h)` and `A^e(6, h)`, the number with an even number of blocks ([[odd-castles-and-block-tables](pages/odd-castles-and-block-tables.md)], section *The odd-block count*)

counts: the number of tree skylines of area `n` (the number of cells) and height at most 3: skylines with every column in `{1, 2, 3}` in which no two neighboring columns both have height at least 2 ([[tree-castle-by-area](pages/tree-castle-by-area.md)]). counts: the number of castles of area `n` (`n` cells), counted up to mirror image, whose sandpile group is trivial ([[sandpile-group](pages/sandpile-group.md)], [[sandpile-census](pages/sandpile-census.md)]). The sandpile group of a castle comes from its castle graph (cells as vertices, joined when they share a side) with sand leaving through a sink, one cell in the sink model and the whole bottom row in the tide model; in both models it is trivial exactly when the castle graph is a tree, that is, for the tree castles, in which no two neighboring columns both have height at least 2. So this counts the tree castles of area `n` up to mirror image, `(A005251(n + 2) + A000931(n + 6))/2` by Burnside's lemma, the palindromic ones numbering `A000931(n + 6)` ([[castle-graph](pages/castle-graph.md)])

counts: the number of palindromic tree castles of area `n`, the number of cells: tree castles, in which no two neighboring columns both have height at least 2 so that the graph of cells sharing a side is a tree, that read the same backwards ([[padovan-families](pages/padovan-families.md)], [[castle-graph](pages/castle-graph.md)]). The tree castles are the castles whose sandpile group is trivial, and the palindromic count enters the count of those castles up to mirror image, `(A005251(n + 2) + A000931(n + 6))/2` ([[sandpile-census](pages/sandpile-census.md)])
oeis_name: Padovan sequence (or Padovan numbers): a(n) = a(n-2) + a(n-3) with a(0) = 1, a(1) = a(2) = 0.

counts: the number of castles of `n` cells, with a castle and its mirror image counted once, whose sandpile group `K_sink` in the sink model is cyclic, a single group `Z/m` (the trivial group included). The sandpile group, also called the critical group, is the finite abelian group of the stable configurations of sand grains that recur when grains topple from cell to cell; in the sink model sand leaves the castle through one cell ([[sandpile-group](pages/sandpile-group.md)], [[sandpile-census](pages/sandpile-census.md)])

the number of different groups, up to isomorphism, that occur as the sink-model sandpile group `K_sink` of a castle of `n` cells; it is a count of groups. The sandpile group, also called the critical group, is the finite abelian group of the stable configurations of sand grains that recur when grains topple from cell to cell; in the sink model sand leaves the castle through one cell ([[sandpile-group](pages/sandpile-group.md)], [[sandpile-census](pages/sandpile-census.md)])

the number of castles of `n` cells, with a castle and its mirror image counted once, whose sandpile group `K_tide` in the tide model is cyclic, a single group `Z/m` (the trivial group included). The sandpile group, also called the critical group, is the finite abelian group of the stable configurations of sand grains that recur when grains topple from cell to cell; in the tide model the whole bottom row serves as the sink ([[sandpile-group](pages/sandpile-group.md)], [[sandpile-census](pages/sandpile-census.md)])

the number of different groups, up to isomorphism, that occur as the tide-model sandpile group `K_tide` of a castle of `n` cells; it is a count of groups. The sandpile group, also called the critical group, is the finite abelian group of the stable configurations of sand grains that recur when grains topple from cell to cell; in the tide model the whole bottom row serves as the sink ([[sandpile-group](pages/sandpile-group.md)], [[sandpile-census](pages/sandpile-census.md)])

the order of the sandpile group, in the sink model, of the 2-wide ladder: the box castle `(2, …, 2)` of width `n` lying down, or `(n, n)` standing up. Grains sit on the cells, a cell holding at least as many grains as it has neighbors topples and sends one grain to each, and grains that reach the sink vanish; the recurrent configurations form the sandpile group, and in the sink model the sink is one cell ([[sandpile-group](pages/sandpile-group.md)]). The order is the number of spanning trees of the `2 × n` grid of cells and the group is cyclic; it is a statistic of one castle for each `n`

the order of the sandpile group, in the tide model, of the box castle `(2, …, 2)` of width `w`, a 2-wide ladder lying down. Grains sit on the cells, a cell holding at least as many grains as it has neighbors topples and sends one grain to each, and grains that reach the sink vanish; the recurrent configurations form the sandpile group, and in the tide model the whole bottom row is the sink ([[sandpile-group](pages/sandpile-group.md)]). Every 2 × 2 square of cells in this castle rests on the bottom row, the group is cyclic, and its order is the even-indexed Fibonacci number `F_{2w}`; it is a statistic of one castle for each `w`
oeis_name: F(2n) = bisection of Fibonacci sequence: a(n) = 3*a(n-1) - a(n-2).

counts: the order of the sandpile group, in the tide model, of the box castle `(h, h)` of height `h`, a 2-wide ladder standing up. Grains sit on the cells, a cell holding at least as many grains as it has neighbors topples and sends one grain to each, and grains that reach the sink vanish; the recurrent configurations form the sandpile group, and in the tide model the whole bottom row is the sink ([[sandpile-group](pages/sandpile-group.md)]). Only the lowest 2 × 2 square of cells in this castle rests on the bottom row, and the group is cyclic; it is a statistic of one castle for each `h`

the number of Fibonacci-word castles of width `w`: Fibonacci castles (height 2, no two neighboring columns of height 2) whose tower, the second row read as a string with 1 for a cell and 0 for an empty place, occurs somewhere in the infinite Fibonacci word `0, 1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 0, 1, …`, the limit of `0 → 01`, `1 → 0` started from `0` ([[fibonacci-castles-sub-families](pages/fibonacci-castles-sub-families.md)]). The Fibonacci word is Sturmian, with exactly `w + 1` distinct pieces of each length `w`, and from `w = 3` none of them is all zeros, so the count is `w + 1` from `w = 3`, growing linearly

the number of balanced castles of width `w`: Fibonacci castles (castles of height 2 with no two neighboring columns of height 2, the same as the tree castles of height 2, [[fibonacci-castle](pages/fibonacci-castle.md)]) whose tower, the 0/1 string left after removing the bottom row, with a 1 for each height-2 column, is balanced, meaning that any two of its factors of equal length contain numbers of 1s differing by at most 1 ([[fibonacci-castles-sub-families](pages/fibonacci-castles-sub-families.md)]). They are half the balanced binary words of length `w`

the number of maximal castles of width `w`: Fibonacci castles (castles of height 2 with no two neighboring columns of height 2) in which no further column can be raised to height 2, so that every gap between height-2 columns is 1 or 2 columns and each end run of height-1 columns has length 0 or 1. Their second rows are the maximal independent sets of the path on `w` vertices, which the Padovan entry A000931 counts, and they grow by width like the plastic number ([[fibonacci-castles-sub-families](pages/fibonacci-castles-sub-families.md)])
note: (the entry counts the maximal independent vertex sets of the path graph)
oeis_name: Padovan sequence (or Padovan numbers): a(n) = a(n-2) + a(n-3) with a(0) = 1, a(1) = a(2) = 0.

counts: the number of spaced castles of width `w`: Fibonacci castles (castles of height 2 with no two neighboring columns of height 2) whose height-2 columns are at least 3 apart, so that the tower, the 0/1 string left after removing the bottom row, has no `101` [[fibonacci-castles-sub-families](pages/fibonacci-castles-sub-families.md)]; they are supergolden by width
note: ; the bijection with the Fibonacci castles of `w + 1` cells is on the page
oeis_name: Expansion of 1/((1-x)*(1-x-x^3)).

counts: the number of `(1, 3)`-RLL castles of width `w`: Fibonacci castles (castles of height 2 with no two neighboring columns of height 2) whose tower, the 0/1 string left after removing the bottom row, with a 1 for each column of height 2, is `(1, 3)`-run-length-limited, with runs of 0s between successive 1s at least 1 long, which every Fibonacci castle has, and every run of 0s, the end runs included, at most 3 long [[fibonacci-castles-sub-families](pages/fibonacci-castles-sub-families.md)]. The `(1, 3)` constraint is the one used in flexible disk drives (MFM)
note: (for `w ≥ 4` and `A003410(w) − 1` for `w ≤ 3`; the entry counts the binary words with no `11` and no `0000`, the towers); [A226136](https://oeis.org/A226136), whose terms equal the castle counts
oeis_name: Expansion of (1+x)(1+x^2)/(1-x-x^3).

counts: the number of `(1, 7)`-RLL castles of width `w`: Fibonacci castles (castles of height 2 with no two neighboring columns of height 2) whose tower, the 0/1 string left after removing the bottom row, with a 1 for each column of height 2, is `(1, 7)`-run-length-limited, with runs of 0s between successive 1s at least 1 long, which every Fibonacci castle has, and every run of 0s, the end runs included, at most 7 long [[fibonacci-castles-sub-families](pages/fibonacci-castles-sub-families.md)]. The `(1, 7)` constraint is the one used in magnetic tape

the number of `(2, 7)`-RLL castles of width `w`: Fibonacci castles (castles of height 2 with no two neighboring columns of height 2) whose tower, the 0/1 string left after removing the bottom row, with a 1 for each column of height 2, is `(2, 7)`-run-length-limited, with runs of 0s between successive 1s at least 2 long, and every run of 0s, the end runs included, at most 7 long [[fibonacci-castles-sub-families](pages/fibonacci-castles-sub-families.md)]. The `(2, 7)` constraint is the one used in magnetic tape

the number of `(2, 10)`-RLL castles of width `w`: Fibonacci castles (castles of height 2 with no two neighboring columns of height 2) whose tower, the 0/1 string left after removing the bottom row, with a 1 for each column of height 2, is `(2, 10)`-run-length-limited, with runs of 0s between successive 1s at least 2 long, and every run of 0s, the end runs included, at most 10 long [[fibonacci-castles-sub-families](pages/fibonacci-castles-sub-families.md)]. The `(2, 10)` constraint is the one used in CDs and DVDs

the width of the von Neumann castle `vN(n)`, the castle of the ordinal `n = {0, 1, …, n − 1}`, where the castle of a set is a bottom block carrying the castles of its members left to right with one empty column between neighbors, for example `vN(2) = (2, 1, 3)` ([[von-neumann-castles](pages/von-neumann-castles.md)]). It is a statistic of one castle for each `n`; `vN(0) = (1)` has width 1
oeis_name: a(n) = 2^n - 1. (Sometimes called Mersenne numbers, although that name is usually reserved for A001348.)

counts: the area, the number of cells, of the von Neumann castle `vN(n)`, the castle of the ordinal `n = {0, 1, …, n − 1}`, where the castle of a set is a bottom block carrying the castles of its members left to right with one empty column between neighbors, for example `vN(2) = (2, 1, 3)` ([[von-neumann-castles](pages/von-neumann-castles.md)]). It is a statistic of one castle for each `n`

the number of blocks (a block being a maximal run of cells in one row) of the von Neumann castle `vN(n)`, the castle of the ordinal `n = {0, 1, …, n − 1}`, where the castle of a set is a bottom block carrying the castles of its members left to right with one empty column between neighbors, for example `vN(2) = (2, 1, 3)` ([[von-neumann-castles](pages/von-neumann-castles.md)]), with `C(n, d)` of them in row `d + 1`, the nodes of the binomial tree of order `n`. It is a statistic of one castle for each `n`; since `2^n` is even for `n ≥ 1`, every `vN(n)` from `n = 1` has an even number of blocks
formula: `2^n`, the nodes of the binomial tree of order `n`
oeis_name: Powers of 2: a(n) = 2^n.

counts: the column heights of one infinite skyline, whose first `2^n − 1` columns are the von Neumann castle `vN(n)`, the castle of the ordinal `n = {0, 1, …, n − 1}`, where the castle of a set is a bottom block carrying the castles of its members left to right with one empty column between neighbors, for example `vN(2) = (2, 1, 3)` ([[von-neumann-castles](pages/von-neumann-castles.md)]) for every `n ≥ 1`. It lists the columns of a single skyline: column `i` has height `s_2(i) + (i mod 2)`, with `s_2(i)` the number of 1s in the binary form of `i`
formula: `s_2(i) + (i mod 2)`, with `s_2` the binary weight A000120

counts: the number of alternating castles with `b` blocks, castles of odd width with `c_1 > c_2 < c_3 > ⋯ < c_w`. Each is the castle of exactly one plane tree with `b` nodes, its block tree, in which the children of a block are the blocks standing on it ([[von-neumann-castles](pages/von-neumann-castles.md)]); the castles of hereditarily finite sets are among them, `A004111(b)` of them with `b` blocks
oeis_name: Catalan numbers: C(n) = binomial(2n,n)/(n+1) = (2n)!/(n!(n+1)!).

counts: the number of castles of hereditarily finite sets with `b` blocks, a block being a maximal run of cells in one row. A hereditarily finite set is a finite set whose members are hereditarily finite, down to the empty set. Its castle is a bottom block carrying the castles of its members from left to right, in increasing Ackermann code, one empty column between neighbors, and the empty set's castle is the single cell `(1)` ([[von-neumann-castles](pages/von-neumann-castles.md)]). Distinct sets have distinct castles and each block is one pair of braces of the set written out in full, so these are the sets with `b` pairs of braces, the rooted identity trees with `b` nodes
oeis_name: Number of rooted identity trees with n nodes (rooted trees whose automorphism group is the identity group).

counts: the number of blocks of the Ackermann castle `ack(m)`, a block being a maximal run of cells in one row. The Ackermann castle `ack(m)` is the castle of the hereditarily finite set with Ackermann code `m`, the set whose members are the sets coded by the positions of the 1s in the binary form of `m`; the castle is a bottom block carrying the castles of the members from left to right in increasing code, one empty column between neighbors, and the empty set's castle is the single cell `(1)` ([[von-neumann-castles](pages/von-neumann-castles.md)]). It is a statistic of one castle for each `m`, equal to the number of pairs of braces in the set written out in full
formula: `1 + Σ blocks(ack(k))` over the positions `k` of the binary 1s of `m`

counts: the width of the Ackermann castle `ack(m)`. The Ackermann castle `ack(m)` is the castle of the hereditarily finite set with Ackermann code `m`, the set whose members are the sets coded by the positions of the 1s in the binary form of `m`; the castle is a bottom block carrying the castles of the members from left to right in increasing code, one empty column between neighbors, and the empty set's castle is the single cell `(1)` ([[von-neumann-castles](pages/von-neumann-castles.md)]). It is a statistic of one castle for each `m`: the width is `2·leaves(m) − 1`, with `leaves(m)` the number of leaves of the set's membership tree, the base-2 digital convolution sequence A033922(`m`)
oeis_name: Base-2 digital convolution sequence.

counts: the height of the Ackermann castle `ack(m)`. The Ackermann castle `ack(m)` is the castle of the hereditarily finite set with Ackermann code `m`, the set whose members are the sets coded by the positions of the 1s in the binary form of `m`; the castle is a bottom block carrying the castles of the members from left to right in increasing code, one empty column between neighbors, and the empty set's castle is the single cell `(1)` ([[von-neumann-castles](pages/von-neumann-castles.md)]). It is a statistic of one castle for each `m`: the height is 1 plus the rank of the set, which is the iterated base-2 logarithm A010096(`m`), also `1 + A230864(m + 1)`
oeis_name: log2*(n) (version 1): number of times floor(log_2(x)) is used in floor(log_2(floor(log_2(...(floor(log_2(n)))...)))) = 0.

counts: the numbers `m`, in increasing order, whose Ackermann castle `ack(m)` has an even number of blocks, a block being a maximal run of cells in one row. The Ackermann castle `ack(m)` is the castle of the hereditarily finite set with Ackermann code `m`, the set whose members are the sets coded by the positions of the 1s in the binary form of `m`; the castle is a bottom block carrying the castles of the members from left to right in increasing code, one empty column between neighbors, and the empty set's castle is the single cell `(1)` ([[von-neumann-castles](pages/von-neumann-castles.md)]). These are the numbers missing from A372325, and they include the codes 1, 3 and 11 of the ordinals 1, 2 and 3
formula: the complement of A372325: an odd number of the binary 1s of `m` at positions with odd-block castles

counts: the numbers `m`, in increasing order, whose Ackermann castle `ack(m)` has an odd number of blocks, a block being a maximal run of cells in one row, which are the `m` with A116549(`m`) odd. The Ackermann castle `ack(m)` is the castle of the hereditarily finite set with Ackermann code `m`, the set whose members are the sets coded by the positions of the 1s in the binary form of `m`; the castle is a bottom block carrying the castles of the members from left to right in increasing code, one empty column between neighbors, and the empty set's castle is the single cell `(1)` ([[von-neumann-castles](pages/von-neumann-castles.md)]). They are the terms of A372325, the numbers whose binary form has an even number of 1s at positions that are themselves terms
formula: an even number of the binary 1s of `m` at positions with odd-block castles
oeis_name: Numbers whose binary expansion has an even number of 1's among positions listed in this sequence.

counts: the number of brick-wall castles (castles on the hexagonal tiling read as a brick wall: a full bottom row of `w` bricks, every higher brick resting on both bricks below it, a block being a maximal run of bricks in one row, [[brick-wall-castles](pages/brick-wall-castles.md)]) of width `w`, the bottom-row length; they are the fountains of coins counted by bottom row
oeis_name: Catalan numbers: C(n) = binomial(2n,n)/(n+1) = (2n)!/(n!(n+1)!).

counts: the number of brick-wall castles ([[brick-wall-castles](pages/brick-wall-castles.md)], castles on the brick wall whose every higher brick rests on both bricks below it) of width `w` (bottom row of `w` bricks) and height exactly `h` (`h` rows of bricks); they correspond to the Dyck paths of semilength `w` and height `h`
formula: the Dyck paths of semilength `w` and height `h`, by the up-step levels
oeis_name: Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) is the number of Dyck paths of semilength n and height k (1 <= k <= n).

counts: the number of brick-wall castles ([[brick-wall-castles](pages/brick-wall-castles.md)], castles on the brick wall whose every higher brick rests on both bricks below it) of width `w` (bottom row of `w` bricks) with `b` blocks, a block being a maximal run of bricks in one row: the Narayana numbers `N(w, b)`, since a castle with `b` blocks matches a Dyck path of semilength `w` with `w + 1 − b` peaks
