note: (Narayana numbers; blocks = `w + 1 −` peaks of the Dyck path)
oeis_name: Triangle of Narayana numbers T(n,k) = C(n-1,k-1)*C(n,k-1)/k with 1 <= k <= n, read by rows. Also called the Catalan triangle.

counts: the number of brick-wall castles ([[brick-wall-castles](pages/brick-wall-castles.md)], castles on the brick wall whose every higher brick rests on both bricks below it) of width `w` (bottom row of `w` bricks) with an even number of blocks, over all heights; they are equinumerous with the plane trees with an even number of leaves
note: (plane trees with an even number of leaves)
oeis_name: Number of plane trees with even number of leaves.

counts: the signed count `S_brick(w)` of the brick-wall castles ([[brick-wall-castles](pages/brick-wall-castles.md)], castles on the brick wall whose every higher brick rests on both bricks below it) of width `w`, over all heights: the number with an even number of blocks minus the number with an odd number, `Σ(−1)^blocks`. It is 0 at even width and is read off the Dyck paths counted by peaks at `t = −1`
formula: `0` (`w` even), `(−1)^{(w+1)/2} C_{(w−1)/2}` (`w` odd), from the Dyck paths by peaks at `t = −1`

counts: the number of brick-wall castles ([[brick-wall-castles](pages/brick-wall-castles.md)], castles on the brick wall whose every higher brick rests on both bricks below it) of semi-perimeter `s = w + b`, the width plus the number of blocks, which is the semi-perimeter (half the boundary length) of the square-grid castle that the brick-wall castle shears to; that shear gives the castles whose columns drop by at most 1 and end at height 1, which are counted by the peakless Motzkin paths
note: (peakless Motzkin paths; the shear of the drops of at most 1, last column at height 1, of the Motzkin section)
oeis_name: Generalized Catalan numbers: a(n+1) = a(n) + Sum_{k=1..n-1} a(k)*a(n-1-k).

counts: the number of brick-wall castles ([[brick-wall-castles](pages/brick-wall-castles.md)], castles on the brick wall whose every higher brick rests on both bricks below it) with `n` cells, the bricks; they are the fountains of `n` coins, counted by Odlyzko and Wilf's continued fraction
formula: `1/(1 − x/(1 − x²/(1 − x³/⋯)))`, Odlyzko and Wilf's continued fraction
oeis_name: Number of fountains of n coins.

counts: the number of brick-wall castles ([[brick-wall-castles](pages/brick-wall-castles.md)], castles on the brick wall whose every higher brick rests on both bricks below it) of width `w` (bottom row of `w` bricks) and height exactly 2
oeis_name: a(n) = 2^n - 1. (Sometimes called Mersenne numbers, although that name is usually reserved for A001348.)

counts: the number `A^e_brick(w, 2)` of brick-wall castles ([[brick-wall-castles](pages/brick-wall-castles.md)], castles on the brick wall whose every higher brick rests on both bricks below it) of width `w` and height exactly 2 with an even number of blocks; after the shear, these have an odd number of runs of height-2 columns after the first column
note: (an odd number of runs of 2s after the first column)
oeis_name: Sum of every 4th entry of row n in Pascal's triangle, starting at binomial(n,2).

counts: the signed count `S_brick(w, 2)` of the brick-wall castles ([[brick-wall-castles](pages/brick-wall-castles.md)], castles on the brick wall whose every higher brick rests on both bricks below it) of width `w` and height exactly 2: the number with an even number of blocks minus the number with an odd number
oeis_name: Expansion of 1/((1 - 2*x + 2*x^2)*(1-x)).

counts: the number `A^e_brick(w, 3)` of brick-wall castles ([[brick-wall-castles](pages/brick-wall-castles.md)], castles on the brick wall whose every higher brick rests on both bricks below it) of width `w` and height exactly 3 with an even number of blocks

the number `A^e_brick(w, 4)` of brick-wall castles ([[brick-wall-castles](pages/brick-wall-castles.md)], castles on the brick wall whose every higher brick rests on both bricks below it) of width `w` and height exactly 4 with an even number of blocks

the number of block fountains of width `w`: the brick-wall castles ([[brick-wall-castles](pages/brick-wall-castles.md)], castles on the brick wall whose every higher brick rests on both bricks below it) with one block per row, each row a single unbroken run of bricks. Sheared onto the square grid they are the convex 1-histograms, castles that start at height 1, rise by at most 1 per column, and rise then fall

the number of keystone castles of width `w`, any height: castles on the triangular tiling with a full bottom row of `w` up triangles and the `w − 1` down triangles between them, every higher triangle supported so that nothing overhangs ([[keystone-castles](pages/keystone-castles.md)]); the top outline of each is a large Schröder path of semilength `w − 1`, a path of up, down and flat steps that never goes below its base line
note: (large Schröder numbers; Bala's stacks of large Schröder type)
oeis_name: Large Schröder numbers (or large Schroeder numbers, or big Schroeder numbers).

counts: the number of keystone castles of width `w` (`w` up triangles in the bottom row), any height, with `b` blocks, a block being a maximal run of triangles in one row ([[keystone-castles](pages/keystone-castles.md)])
oeis_name: Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) = C(n+k,n)*C(n,k)/(k+1), for n >= 0, k = 0..n.

counts: the number of keystone castles (castles on the triangular tiling with a full bottom row of `w` up triangles and the `w − 1` down triangles between them, every higher triangle supported so that nothing overhangs, [[keystone-castles](pages/keystone-castles.md)]), any width and height, whose width plus number of blocks is `s`, a block being a maximal run of triangles in one row. Reading the outline's large Schröder path with every step of length 1 makes these the Motzkin paths of length `s − 2`
oeis_name: Motzkin numbers: number of ways of drawing any number of nonintersecting chords joining n (labeled) points on a circle.

counts: the number of keystone castles of width `w` and height 2, two rows of triangles ([[keystone-castles](pages/keystone-castles.md)])
oeis_name: a(n) = Fibonacci(2*n + 1) - 1.

counts: the number of keystone castles with `n` cells, a cell being one triangle, any width and height ([[keystone-castles](pages/keystone-castles.md)])
note: (Bala's fraction of the stacks of large Schröder type at `b = q`)
oeis_name: Expansion of 1/(1 - q^2 - q^3/(1 - q^4 - q^5/(1 - q^6 - q^7/(1 - q^8 - q^9/(1 - ... ))))), a continued fraction.

counts: the number of keystone castles of width `w` and height 3, three rows of triangles (castles on the triangular tiling with a full bottom row of `w` up triangles and the `w − 1` down triangles between them, every higher triangle supported so that nothing overhangs, [[keystone-castles](pages/keystone-castles.md)]). Their outlines are the large Schröder paths of semilength `w − 1` and height exactly 2, paths of up, down and flat steps that never go below their base line; `Sch_k` in the formula counts those of height at most `k`

the number of keystone castles of width `w`, any height, with an even number of blocks minus the number with an odd number, written `S_key(w)`, a block being a maximal run of triangles in one row (castles on the triangular tiling with a full bottom row of `w` up triangles and the `w − 1` down triangles between them, every higher triangle supported so that nothing overhangs, [[keystone-castles](pages/keystone-castles.md)]). It is −1 at `w = 1`, the single triangle, and 0 for every `w ≥ 2`: exactly half the keystone castles of each larger width have an even number of blocks

the number of keystone castles of width `w` and height 2 with an even number of blocks minus the number with an odd number, written `S_key(w, 2)`, a block being a maximal run of triangles in one row (castles on the triangular tiling with a full bottom row of `w` up triangles and the `w − 1` down triangles between them, every higher triangle supported so that nothing overhangs, [[keystone-castles](pages/keystone-castles.md)]); it repeats `0, 1, 2, 2, 1, 0` with period 6
formula: period 6, from `−x(1 − x²)/(1 + x³) + x/(1 − x)`

counts: the number of keystone castles of width `w` and height 2 with an even number of blocks, written `A^e_key(w, 2)`, a block being a maximal run of triangles in one row (castles on the triangular tiling with a full bottom row of `w` up triangles and the `w − 1` down triangles between them, every higher triangle supported so that nothing overhangs, [[keystone-castles](pages/keystone-castles.md)]). This is the keystone version of the Project Euler 502 count, half of the `F_{2w−1} − 1` keystone castles of height 2 plus half the even-minus-odd difference `S_key(w, 2)`

the number of keystone castles of width `w` and height 3 with an even number of blocks, written `A^e_key(w, 3)`, a block being a maximal run of triangles in one row (castles on the triangular tiling with a full bottom row of `w` up triangles and the `w − 1` down triangles between them, every higher triangle supported so that nothing overhangs, [[keystone-castles](pages/keystone-castles.md)]); the first ones have width 4

the number of keystone castles of height 2, any width, with `n` cells, a cell being one triangle (castles on the triangular tiling with a full bottom row of `w` up triangles and the `w − 1` down triangles between them, every higher triangle supported so that nothing overhangs, [[keystone-castles](pages/keystone-castles.md)]); the smallest has 4 cells, three in the bottom row and one up triangle on top
growth: `1.40127`, a Salem number, `z⁶ − z⁴ − z³ − z² + 1`

counts: the number of keystone castles of height 2 whose width plus number of blocks is `s`, a block being a maximal run of triangles in one row (castles on the triangular tiling with a full bottom row of `w` up triangles and the `w − 1` down triangles between them, every higher triangle supported so that nothing overhangs, [[keystone-castles](pages/keystone-castles.md)])
oeis_name: a(n) = 2^n - 1. (Sometimes called Mersenne numbers, although that name is usually reserved for A001348.)

counts: the denominators of the Jacobi-Perron convergents of `2ψ² = 3.5098…`, with `ψ` the plastic number. `2ψ²` is the largest root of the characteristic polynomial of the linear recurrence that the signed tower count `P(6, L)` (the sum of `(−1)^{blocks}` over the towers of height at most 6 on a base of length `L`) satisfies in `L`. The Jacobi-Perron algorithm is a continued fraction for the pair `(ρ, ρ²)`, and its expansion of `2ψ²` is periodic. It is not a castle count ([[castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk](pages/castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk.md)])

the number of rectangles of `n` cells, one `a × b` rectangle for each divisor `a` of `n`, so the number of divisors of `n`. A rectangle standing on its bottom row is a box castle, a castle whose columns all have the same height, so this counts the box castles of area `n`, the area being the number of cells. It is the most restricted of the nine polyomino families counted by number of cells in the table on [[convex-polyomino-by-area](pages/convex-polyomino-by-area.md)]
oeis_name: d(n) (also called tau(n) or sigma_0(n)), the number of divisors of n.

counts: the number of partitions of `n` into distinct parts. It counts castles: the Euler castles (castles whose columns fall by 0 or 1 at each step and end at height 1, such as `(3, 3, 2, 1, 1)`, [[euler-castles](pages/euler-castles.md)]) of area `n`, the number of cells, since the rows of an Euler castle are a partition of its area into distinct parts. On [[multiset-partitions](pages/multiset-partitions.md)] it is Bender's count `c*` for one element repeated `n` times: the partitions of that multiset with no two blocks equal are the partitions of `n` into distinct parts
oeis_name: Expansion of Product_{m >= 1} (1 + x^m); number of partitions of n into distinct parts; number of partitions of n into odd parts.

counts: the Lucas numbers `L_n`, `2, 1, 3, 4, 7, 11, …`, the companions of the Fibonacci numbers (the same recurrence started from 2 and 1). It is not a castle count. It enters through the golden mean `φ`, the growth rate by width of the Fibonacci castles (castles of height 2 with no two neighboring columns of height 2): `L_n = φ^n + (−1/φ)^n` is the trace sequence that goes with the convergents of the continued fraction `[1; 1, 1, …]` of `φ` ([[castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk](pages/castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk.md)], [[metallic-means](pages/metallic-means.md)])
oeis_name: Lucas numbers beginning at 2: L(n) = L(n-1) + L(n-2), L(0) = 2, L(1) = 1.

counts: the number of Ferrers diagrams of `n` cells: columns standing on one baseline with weakly decreasing heights, the same as the partitions of `n`. Every Ferrers diagram is a castle, a Ferrers castle, so this counts the Ferrers castles of area `n`, the area being the number of cells. It is one of the nine polyomino families counted by number of cells in the table on [[convex-polyomino-by-area](pages/convex-polyomino-by-area.md)]
oeis_name: a(n) is the number of partitions of n (the partition numbers).

counts: the Fibonacci numbers `F_n`. They count castles in several ways: the Fibonacci castles (castles of height 2 with no two neighboring columns of height 2, the same as the tree castles of height 2, [[fibonacci-castle](pages/fibonacci-castle.md)]) of width `w` number `F_{w+2} − 1` (see A000071); the castles of height 2 and area `A`, the number of cells, number `F_{A+1} − 1`; and the Euler castles (columns falling by 0 or 1 at each step to height 1) of semi-perimeter `s`, the width plus the number of blocks, number `F_{s−1}` ([[euler-castles](pages/euler-castles.md)])
oeis_name: Fibonacci numbers: F(n) = F(n-1) + F(n-2) with F(0) = 0 and F(1) = 1.

counts: the powers of 2. They count castles: all castles of area `n`, the number of cells, number `2^{n−1}`, since a castle of area `n` is a composition of `n`, its column heights in order ([[oeis-mining-pe502](pages/oeis-mining-pe502.md)]); the Kolmogorov castles of width `2n + 1` and height 2 number `2^n` ([[kolmogorov-castles](pages/kolmogorov-castles.md)]); and the von Neumann castle `vN(n)` has `2^n` blocks, a block being a maximal run of cells in one row ([[von-neumann-castles](pages/von-neumann-castles.md)]). On towers, what is left of a castle after removing its bottom row, the sum of `(−1)^{blocks}` over the towers of height at most 2 on a base of length `L` whose last column has even height is `P_even(2, L) = 2^L` ([[tower-parity-sectors](pages/tower-parity-sectors.md)])
oeis_name: Powers of 2: a(n) = 2^n.

counts: the number of castles of height exactly 3 and area `n`, the number of cells. A castle of area `n` is a composition of `n`, its column heights in order, and these are the compositions of `n` with largest part 3 ([[castles-of-height-h-by-area](pages/castles-of-height-h-by-area.md)]). Writing each column of height `c` as a run of `c − 1` 1s, with single 0s between columns, matches them with the binary strings of length `n − 1` whose longest run of 1s has length 2 ([[balado-silvestre-2026-runs-binary-strings](pages/balado-silvestre-2026-runs-binary-strings.md)])
oeis_name: a(n) is the number of compositions of n in which the maximal part is 3.

counts: the number of castles of height exactly 4 and area `n`, the number of cells. A castle of area `n` is a composition of `n`, its column heights in order, and these are the compositions of `n` with largest part 4 ([[castles-of-height-h-by-area](pages/castles-of-height-h-by-area.md)]); writing each column of height `c` as a run of `c − 1` 1s, with single 0s between columns, matches them with the binary strings of length `n − 1` whose longest run of 1s has length 3 ([[balado-silvestre-2026-runs-binary-strings](pages/balado-silvestre-2026-runs-binary-strings.md)])
oeis_name: a(n) = number of compositions of n in which the maximum part size is 4.

counts: the Bell numbers `B(n)`, the number of ways to partition a set of `n` elements into blocks (a block here is one part of the partition, a different sense from a castle block). It is not a castle count. It appears on [[multiset-partitions](pages/multiset-partitions.md)] and [[bender-1974-partitions-of-multisets](pages/bender-1974-partitions-of-multisets.md)] as the case of `n` distinct elements, where all four of Bender's multiset-partition counts equal `B(n)`, and as the base of Bender's asymptotic for multisets with repeated elements
oeis_name: Bell or exponential numbers: number of ways to partition a set of n labeled elements.

counts: the binary weight `s_2(j)`, the number of 1s in the binary form of `j`. It is a statistic of single castles, the von Neumann castles (the castles of the ordinals `n = {0, 1, …, n − 1}`, [[von-neumann-castles](pages/von-neumann-castles.md)]): their even-numbered columns have heights `c_{2j} = s_2(j)`, and their odd-numbered ones `c_{2j+1} = s_2(j) + 2`
oeis_name: Ones-counting sequence: number of 1's in binary expansion of n (or the binary weight of n).

counts: the number of unimodal skylines of height at most 2 and width `w`, skylines `(c_1, …, c_w)` with every `c_i` in `{1, 2}` that weakly rise and then weakly fall, `1 + C(w + 1, 2)` of them: the skyline of all 1s, which is not a castle of height 2, plus the `C(w + 1, 2)` convex castles of height 2, whose second row is one unbroken run. On [[tower-spacing-castles](pages/tower-spacing-castles.md)] it is the limit `g → ∞` of the height-2 row of the skylines with tower spacing at least `g` (in every row, each run of empty cells with filled cells on both sides has length at least `g`), since for `w ≤ g + 1` that rule allows exactly the unimodal skylines
oeis_name: Central polygonal numbers (the Lazy Caterer's sequence): n(n+1)/2 + 1; or, maximal number of pieces formed when slicing a pancake with n cuts.

counts: the factorials `h!`. They count castles: the rainbow castles of height `h`, castles of width `h` whose column heights are a permutation of `{1, …, h}` (every such skyline reaches height `h`), number exactly `h!` ([[castle-classification-shape](pages/castle-classification-shape.md)], [[aocp-permutations](pages/aocp-permutations.md)])
oeis_name: Factorial numbers: n! = 1*2*3*4*...*n (order of symmetric group S_n, number of permutations of n letters).

counts: the triangular numbers `C(w + 1, 2)`. They count castles: the castles of width `w` and height 2 whose second row is a single unbroken run, which are the convex castles of height 2 ([[convex-castle-binomial-identity](pages/convex-castle-binomial-identity.md)]). Each has two blocks, a block being a maximal run of cells in one row, and at width 4 they are all the castles of height 2 with an even number of blocks: `A^e(4, 2) = C(5, 2) = 10`
oeis_name: Triangular numbers: a(n) = binomial(n+1,2) = n*(n+1)/2 = 0 + 1 + 2 + ... + n.

counts: the powers of 4. It is not a castle count. It appears on [[barry-2005-catalan-transform](pages/barry-2005-catalan-transform.md)] as one of Barry's Ballot-transform pairs (his Table 2): the generalized Ballot transform, the Riordan array `(c(x), x c(x)²)` with `c(x)` the Catalan generating function, sends the odd numbers `2n + 1` to `4^n`
oeis_name: Powers of 4: a(n) = 4^n.

counts: the sums `1² + 3² + ⋯ + (2n − 1)²` of the first `n` odd squares. It is not a castle count. It enters through the signed tower count `P(k, L)`, the number of towers (castles with the bottom row removed) of height at most `k` on a base of length `L` with an even number of blocks minus the number with an odd number: at base length 4 and odd tower height, `P(2m + 1, 4) = −4·A000447(m + 1)`, so this sequence is `|P(2m + 1, 4)|/4` ([[signed-tower-k-direction](pages/signed-tower-k-direction.md)])

the number of tournaments on `n` vertices up to isomorphism, a tournament being a complete graph with a direction on every edge. It is not a castle count. The wiki lists it through `n = 8` on [[unique-tournament](pages/unique-tournament.md)] to confirm, by enumerating all tournaments, the unique tournaments A000570 (those determined by their score vectors), which count the tree skylines of height at most 4 and area `n − 1`: skylines on `{1, …, 4}` with no two neighboring columns of height at least 2, which need not reach height 4 ([[tree-castle-by-area](pages/tree-castle-by-area.md)])
oeis_name: Number of outcomes of unlabeled n-team round-robin tournaments.

counts: the number of score vectors of tournaments on `n` vertices, the lists of numbers of wins, up to order, that some tournament (a complete graph with a direction on every edge) realizes. It is not a castle count. It is an upper bound on the unique tournaments A000570, those determined by their score vectors, and equals them through `n = 4` ([[unique-tournament](pages/unique-tournament.md)]); A000570 counts the tree skylines of height at most 4 and area `n − 1`, skylines on `{1, …, 4}` with no two neighboring columns of height at least 2 ([[tree-castle-by-area](pages/tree-castle-by-area.md)])
oeis_name: Number of different score sequences that are possible in an n-team round-robin tournament.

counts: the number of partitions of `n` into distinct odd parts, the same as the self-conjugate partitions of `n`. It is not itself a castle count. Up to sign it is the signed count of the Ferrers castles of area `n`, the castles whose columns weakly decrease (the Ferrers diagrams of the partitions of `n`): each row of a Ferrers castle is one block, so its block count is its height, and the number with an even number of blocks minus the number with an odd number is `(−1)^n A000700(n)`, by conjugation ([[convex-polyomino-by-area](pages/convex-polyomino-by-area.md)]). Over the monotone castles of area `n`, those whose columns weakly decrease or weakly increase, the same difference is `2(−1)^n A000700(n) − Σ_{d|n} (−1)^d` ([[castle-add-a-column-equation](pages/castle-add-a-column-equation.md)])
oeis_name: Expansion of Product_{k>=0} (1 + x^(2k+1)); number of partitions of n into distinct odd parts; number of self-conjugate partitions; number of symmetric Ferrers graphs with n nodes.

counts: the sums `Σ_k C(n, 4k + 3)` of every fourth entry of row `n` of Pascal's triangle, starting at `C(n, 3)`, the member with residue 3 of the order-4 hyperbolic family ([[hyperbolic-sequence-family](pages/hyperbolic-sequence-family.md)]). It is not a castle count. Two of its three siblings are: the castles of width `w` and height 2 with an even number of blocks number `A038505(w + 1)` (residue 2), and those with an odd number `A038503(w + 1) − 1` (residue 0); the four sequences add to `2^n`

Narayana's cows sequence, `a(n) = a(n − 1) + a(n − 3)`. Less 1, it counts castles: the Fibonacci castles (castles of height 2 with no two neighboring columns of height 2, the same as the tree castles of height 2, [[fibonacci-castle](pages/fibonacci-castle.md)]) with `n` cells number `A000930(n + 1) − 1` (see A077868, [[q-fibonacci-castle](pages/q-fibonacci-castle.md)]), and the spaced castles of width `w`, the Fibonacci castles whose height-2 columns are at least 3 apart, number `A000930(w + 2) − 1` ([[fibonacci-castles-sub-families](pages/fibonacci-castles-sub-families.md)]). Without the subtraction, `A000930(A + 1)` counts the tree skylines of height at most 2 and area `A`, which include the skyline of all 1s ([[tree-castle-by-area](pages/tree-castle-by-area.md)])
oeis_name: Narayana's cows sequence: a(0) = a(1) = a(2) = 1; thereafter a(n) = a(n-1) + a(n-3).

counts: Fine's sequence. It is not a castle count. It appears on [[barry-2005-catalan-transform](pages/barry-2005-catalan-transform.md)] in Barry's Table 1 as the Catalan transform of `0^n − (−1)^n`, the sequence `0, 1, −1, 1, −1, …`, where the Catalan transform sends a generating function `A(x)` to `A(x c(x))`, with `c(x)` the Catalan generating function
oeis_name: Fine's sequence (or Fine numbers): number of relations of valence >= 1 on an n-set; also number of ordered rooted trees with n nodes having root of even degree.

counts: the central binomial coefficients `C(2n, n)`. They count castles: the Kolmogorov castles of width `2n + 1`, all heights together (the castles of a merged order of two samples of `n` values each, column `i` one higher than the absolute lead of one sample over the other, [[kolmogorov-castles](pages/kolmogorov-castles.md)]). On [[barry-2005-catalan-transform](pages/barry-2005-catalan-transform.md)] they are the Catalan transform of `2^n` and the Ballot transform of `1^n`, and the aerated binomial transform `b_n = Σ_k C(n, 2k) a_k` sends them to the central trinomial coefficients A002426, the words of up, flat and down steps that return to their starting height
oeis_name: Central binomial coefficients: binomial(2*n,n) = (2*n)!/(n!)^2.

counts: the number of rows of keystone castles set side by side with widths adding up to `k`, the small Schröder numbers. A keystone castle is a castle on the triangular tiling: a full bottom row of up triangles with the down triangles between them, every higher up triangle resting on a down triangle and every down triangle held by the two up triangles beside it ([[keystone-castles](pages/keystone-castles.md)]). Bala calls such a row a triangle stack with `k` up triangles in its bottom row; its top outline is a small Schröder path to `(2k, 0)`, a path of up steps `(1, 1)`, down steps `(1, −1)` and flat steps `(2, 0)` that never goes below the base line and never runs flat along it ([[bala-2019-area-beneath-small-schroder-paths](pages/bala-2019-area-beneath-small-schroder-paths.md)])
oeis_name: Schroeder's second problem (generalized parentheses); also called super-Catalan numbers or little Schroeder numbers.

counts: the number of partial orders on `h` labeled elements. It is not a castle count. It appears in the half-column problem on [[fractional-width-and-height](pages/fractional-width-and-height.md)]: a strip rule is an `h × h` 0/1 matrix saying which heights may stand next to each other ([[castle-strip](pages/castle-strip.md)]), and among the rules with all eigenvalues positive, those whose principal square root has nonnegative entries number 3, 19, 219, 4231, 130023 at heights 2 to 6, exactly the partial orders on the heights; at height 7, 882 of the partial orders have a negative entry
oeis_name: Number of partially ordered sets ("posets") with n labeled elements (or labeled acyclic transitive digraphs).

counts: the denominators of the continued-fraction convergents to `√5`, `0, 1, 4, 17, 72, 305, …`. It is not a castle count. It is also the metallic sequence of `δ_4 = 2 + √5 = φ³`, `x_n = 4x_{n−1} + x_{n−2}`, equal to `F_{3n}/2`, and `δ_4` is the growth rate by width of the ridge castles of height 5, castles whose neighboring columns differ in height unless both have height 5 ([[ridge-castle](pages/ridge-castle.md)]): the ridge strips of height 5 and width `w` number `x_{w+1} + x_w = F_{3w+2}` ([[metallic-strip-realizability](pages/metallic-strip-realizability.md)])
oeis_name: Denominators of continued fraction convergents to sqrt(5).

counts: the numerators of the continued-fraction convergents to `√5 = [2; 4, 4, …]`. It is not a castle count. It stands beside the denominators A001076 in the convergent table of [[castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk](pages/castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk.md)], in the row of the golden mean `φ = (1 + √5)/2`, the growth rate by width of the Fibonacci castles (castles of height 2 with no two neighboring columns of height 2)
oeis_name: Numerators of continued fraction convergents to sqrt(5).

counts: the number of fixed polyominoes of `n` cells, sets of `n` unit squares joined edge to edge, with rotations and reflections counted as different. Every castle of area `n` is one of them. It is the largest of the nine polyomino families counted by number of cells in the table on [[convex-polyomino-by-area](pages/convex-polyomino-by-area.md)]
oeis_name: Number of fixed polyominoes with n cells.

counts: the number of column-convex polyominoes of `n` cells, polyominoes in which every column is one unbroken run of cells; every castle of area `n` is one, since its columns stand on the base row with no gaps. A quarter turn matches them with the board-pile (horizontally convex) polyominoes. It is one of the nine polyomino families counted by number of cells in the table on [[convex-polyomino-by-area](pages/convex-polyomino-by-area.md)]
oeis_name: Number of board-pile polyominoes with n cells.

counts: the taxicab numbers, the sums of two positive cubes in more than one way. The first, `1729 = 1³ + 12³ = 9³ + 10³`, is a castle count: the castles of width 6 and height 4 with an even number of blocks (a block being a maximal run of cells in one row) number `A^e(6, 4) = 1729` ([[hardy-ramanujan-castle](pages/hardy-ramanujan-castle.md)]). No other of the first 15 taxicab numbers equals a count of all, even-block or odd-block castles, `A(w, h)`, `A^e(w, h)` or `A^o(w, h)`, with `w, h ≤ 40`
oeis_name: Taxi-cab numbers: sums of 2 cubes in more than 1 way.

counts: the Narayana numbers `N(L, k) = (1/L) C(L, k) C(L, k − 1)`, the number of Dyck paths of semilength `L` with `k` peaks ([[narayana-numbers](pages/narayana-numbers.md)]). They count towers by blocks: removing the bottom row of a castle, which is one block, leaves a tower, and the towers of any height on a base of length `L` with `b` blocks (a block being a maximal run of cells in one row) number `T̂(L, b) = Σ_k N(L, k) C(b + L − k, L − 1)` ([[tower-heap](pages/tower-heap.md)])
oeis_name: Triangle of Narayana numbers T(n,k) = C(n-1,k-1)*C(n,k-1)/k with 1 <= k <= n, read by rows. Also called the Catalan triangle.

counts: the generalized pentagonal numbers `k(3k ∓ 1)/2`, `k = 0, ±1, ±2, …`. They are not a count. They are the areas of the pentagonal castles, the Euler castles (castles whose columns fall by 0 or 1 at each step and end at height 1, such as `(3, 3, 2, 1, 1)`, [[euler-castles](pages/euler-castles.md)]) that Franklin's move leaves unmatched; the move trades the top row for the diagonal of the slope at the right end and changes the number of blocks by one, so at every other area the Euler castles with an even number of blocks and those with an odd number are equinumerous
oeis_name: Generalized pentagonal numbers: m*(3*m - 1)/2, m = 0, +-1, +-2, +-3, ....

counts: the Pell-Lucas numbers `Q_n`, `1, 1, 3, 7, 17, 41, …`, the numerators of the continued-fraction convergents to `√2` ([[castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk](pages/castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk.md)]). They count strips on three heights: the skylines of width `w` with every column in `{1, 2, 3}` and neighboring columns differing by at most 1, which need not reach height 3, number `A001333(w + 1)` ([[pell-castle-strip](pages/pell-castle-strip.md)]), and so do the ridge strips of height 3 ([[ridge-castle](pages/ridge-castle.md)]). Taking away the `2^w` such skylines on `{1, 2}` leaves the 1-smooth castles of height 3, `A001333(w + 1) − 2^w` of them ([[pell-castle](pages/pell-castle.md)])
oeis_name: Pell-Lucas numbers: numerators of continued fraction convergents to sqrt(2).

counts: the ruler function, the exponent of the highest power of 2 dividing `2j`: `1, 2, 1, 3, 1, 2, 1, 4, …`. It is a statistic of single castles. The von Neumann castles `vN(n)` (the castles of the ordinals `n = {0, 1, …, n − 1}`, [[von-neumann-castles](pages/von-neumann-castles.md)]) are the beginnings of one infinite skyline, which rises by 2 into each odd-numbered column and falls by `A001511(j)` into column `2j`; this sequence lists those falls
oeis_name: The ruler function: exponent of the highest power of 2 dividing 2n. Equivalently, the 2-adic valuation of 2n.

counts: the Perrin numbers, the sums of the `n`-th powers of the three roots of `x³ = x + 1`, whose real root is the plastic number `ψ` ([[plastic-number](pages/plastic-number.md)]). No castle count on the wiki equals them. They are here as the companion of the Padovan numbers A000931, the way the Lucas numbers go with the Fibonacci numbers, and A000931 counts castles ([[padovan-families](pages/padovan-families.md)]): the maximal castles (Fibonacci castles in which no column can be raised), the palindromic tree castles, and the tree castles of area `n` summed with the sign `(−1)^{blocks}`
oeis_name: Perrin sequence (or Perrin numbers, or Ondrej Such sequence): a(n) = a(n-2) + a(n-3) with a(0) = 3, a(1) = 0, a(2) = 2.

counts: the total number of blocks over all towers of height at most 1 on a base of length `L`, `A001792(L − 1) = (L + 1) 2^{L−2}`, an average of `(L + 1)/4` blocks per tower. It is a sum of block counts over the towers. A tower of height at most 1 is what is left of a castle of height at most 2 after removing its bottom row: a binary string of length `L`, whose blocks (a block being a maximal run of cells in one row) are its runs of 1s ([[block-count-constraints](pages/block-count-constraints.md)], [[balado-silvestre-2026-runs-binary-strings](pages/balado-silvestre-2026-runs-binary-strings.md)])

the numerators of `2w C(2w, w)/4^w`, which is `B_{1/2}(box)/h`, the half-order block count of a box castle divided by its height ([[fractional-block-count](pages/fractional-block-count.md)]). It is a statistic of single castles. The fractional block count `B_α` of a castle adds up the amounts by which each column exceeds a weighted average of the columns to its left (the Grunwald-Letnikov fractional difference of order `α`); it is the area at `α = 0` and the block count at `α = 1`. The box castle of width `w` and height `h`, every column of height `h`, has `B_{1/2} = 2hw C(2w, w)/4^w`
oeis_name: Numerators in expansion of (1 - x)^(-3/2).

counts: the even-indexed Fibonacci numbers `F_{2n}`. It is not a castle count. On [[viennot-heap-tower](pages/viennot-heap-tower.md)] it is the series `1/(1 − 3x + x²) = 1 + 3x + 8x² + 21x³ + ⋯` that Cartier-Foata inversion gives for heaps of interval pieces on a base of length 2 (each piece an interval of columns, two pieces dependent when they share a column), counted by number of pieces. The towers on a base of length 2 (castles with the bottom row removed) with `b` blocks number `2b + 1` (A005408); the two agree for 0 and 1 pieces and part at 2, 8 heaps against 5 towers, so heaps of intervals overcount towers
oeis_name: F(2n) = bisection of Fibonacci sequence: a(n) = 3*a(n-1) - a(n-2).

counts: the even-indexed Fibonacci numbers `m_w = F_{2w}`, one of the two numbers that give the sandpile group of the castle `(3, …, 3)` of height 3 and width `w` in the sink model, where sand leaves through one cell ([[sandpile-group](pages/sandpile-group.md)]). It is not a castle count. By Appendix A of Dhar, Ruelle, Sen and Verma that group is `Z/d_1 × Z/d_2` with `d_2 = gcd(m_w, n_w)`, `d_1 = m_w n_w / d_2` and `n_w = A004254(w)` ([[dhar-ruelle-sen-verma-1995-algebraic-aspects](pages/dhar-ruelle-sen-verma-1995-algebraic-aspects.md)]); `m_w` is also the order of the group of the ladder `(2, …, 2)` of width `w` in the tide model, where sand leaves through the whole bottom row ([[sandpile-census](pages/sandpile-census.md)])
oeis_name: F(2n) = bisection of Fibonacci sequence: a(n) = 3*a(n-1) - a(n-2).

counts: the upper Wythoff sequence `⌊kφ²⌋ = 2, 5, 7, 10, 13, …`. It is not a count. It lists the positions, counted from 1, of the height-2 columns in the Fibonacci castles (castles of height 2 with no two neighboring columns of height 2) whose towers are prefixes of the infinite Fibonacci word, the tower being the 0/1 string left after removing the bottom row ([[fibonacci-castle](pages/fibonacci-castle.md)], [[fibonacci-castles-sub-families](pages/fibonacci-castles-sub-families.md)])
oeis_name: Upper Wythoff sequence (a Beatty sequence): a(n) = floor(n*phi^2), where phi = (1+sqrt(5))/2.

counts: the companion Pell numbers `2, 2, 6, 14, 34, …`, twice the Pell-Lucas numbers A001333. It is not a castle count. It is the trace sequence `δ_2^n + δ̂_2^n` of the silver mean `δ_2 = 1 + √2` and its conjugate `δ̂_2 = 1 − √2` ([[metallic-means](pages/metallic-means.md)], [[castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk](pages/castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk.md)]); the silver mean is the growth rate by width of the ridge castles of height 3 and of the skylines on `{1, 2, 3}` whose neighboring columns differ by at most 1 ([[pell-numbers](pages/pell-numbers.md)])
oeis_name: Companion Pell numbers: a(n) = 2*a(n-1) + a(n-2), a(0) = a(1) = 2.

counts: the central trinomial coefficients, the number of words of `n` steps up, flat or down that end at their starting height, with no floor ([[aocp-multinomial-coefficients](pages/aocp-multinomial-coefficients.md)]); the Motzkin paths are the ones that never go below the start. It counts castles: the cyclic 1-smooth castles of height `h` and width `w`, castles whose neighboring columns differ by at most 1 and whose last column is within 1 of the first, number `A002426(w)` for `w ≤ 2h − 1` and `A002426(2h) − 2h` at `w = 2h` ([[1-smooth-castles](pages/1-smooth-castles.md)])
oeis_name: Central trinomial coefficients: largest coefficient of (1 + x + x^2)^n.

counts: the numerators of the generalized binomial coefficients `C(1/2, k)`, the coefficients of `√(1 + x)`. It is not a castle count. In absolute value they are the numerators of the half-order Grunwald-Letnikov weights `1, −1/2, −1/8, −1/16, −5/128, …`, the weights that the fractional block count `B_{1/2}` gives the columns to the left of each column of a skyline ([[fractional-block-count](pages/fractional-block-count.md)])
oeis_name: Numerators in expansion of sqrt(1+x). Absolute values give numerators in expansion of sqrt(1-x).

counts: the number of towers of height at most 1 on a base of length `L` with at least 2 blocks. A tower of height at most 1 is what is left of a castle of height at most 2 after removing its bottom row: a binary string of length `L`, whose blocks (a block being a maximal run of cells in one row) are its runs of 1s. The bottom row is one more block, so these are also the castles of width `L` and height 2 with at least 3 blocks ([[block-count-constraints](pages/block-count-constraints.md)])

the number of towers of height at most 1 on a base of length `L` with at least 3 blocks. A tower of height at most 1 is what is left of a castle of height at most 2 after removing its bottom row: a binary string of length `L`, whose blocks (a block being a maximal run of cells in one row) are its runs of 1s. The bottom row is one more block, so these are also the castles of width `L` and height 2 with at least 4 blocks ([[block-count-constraints](pages/block-count-constraints.md)])

Bender's `c((0, n))`, the number of partitions of the multiset in which each of `n` elements appears twice, with no two blocks equal and no element repeated inside a block (a block here is one part of the partition), also called the bicoverings of an `n`-set. It is not a castle count. It opens the table of multiset-partition totals on [[multiset-partitions](pages/multiset-partitions.md)], whose link to castles is the one-element case: for one element repeated `n` times, Bender's counts give the partitions of `n`, which count the Ferrers castles of area `n`, and the partitions of `n` into distinct parts, which count the Euler castles of area `n`
oeis_name: Number of bicoverings of an n-set.

counts: the Carmichael numbers `561, 1105, 1729, 2465, …`, the composite numbers `k` with `a^{k−1} ≡ 1 (mod k)` for every `a` coprime to `k`. It is not a castle count; it appears because its first four terms are castle counts, the only ones a search of the first 33 Carmichael numbers finds: `561 = A^o(3, 34)`, the number of castles of width 3 and height 34 with an odd number of blocks; `1105 = A(4, 7)` and `2465 = A(4, 9)`, all castles of width 4 and heights 7 and 9; and `1729 = A^e(6, 4)`, the castles of width 6 and height 4 with an even number of blocks ([[hardy-ramanujan-castle](pages/hardy-ramanujan-castle.md)])
oeis_name: Carmichael numbers.

counts: the number of acyclic directed graphs on `n` labeled vertices. It is not a castle count; it appears in the half-column problem of [[fractional-width-and-height](pages/fractional-width-and-height.md)], which asks which strip rules (the `h × h` 0/1 matrices `M` that say which column heights may stand next to each other, [[castle-strip](pages/castle-strip.md)]) are the square `R^2` of another rule. The rules on `h` heights with all eigenvalues real and positive are exactly the matrices `I + N` with `N` the adjacency matrix of an acyclic directed graph, so they number `A003024(h)`: 3, 25, 543 at heights 2, 3, 4
oeis_name: Number of acyclic digraphs (or DAGs) with n labeled nodes.

counts: the numbers that are sums of three positive cubes. It is not a castle count; [[sum-of-three-cubes-castles](pages/sum-of-three-cubes-castles.md)] tests which castle counts lie in it. Of the 552 values below `10^8` of `A^e(w, h)` with `w ≥ 4`, the number of castles of width `w` and height `h` with an even number of blocks, 56 are sums of three positive cubes, close to the 55.7 expected from the density of the sequence; for example `A^e(4, 2) = 1 + 1 + 8`, `A^e(6, 3) = 27 + 64 + 216` and `A^e(5, 8) = 13^3 + 14^3 + 16^3`
oeis_name: Numbers that are the sum of 3 positive cubes.

counts: the binary reflected Gray code, the order of the `n`-bit numbers in which each differs from the one before in one bit (Knuth's Algorithm G of TAOCP section 7.2.1.1). It is not a castle count; it is the model for listing castles so that each step changes one column, which lets the block parity be updated as the list goes ([[aocp-generating-permutations-tuples](pages/aocp-generating-permutations-tuples.md)], [[castle-gray-code](pages/castle-gray-code.md)])
oeis_name: Decimal equivalent of Gray code for n.

counts: the numbers that are sums of two positive cubes. It is not a castle count; [[sum-of-three-cubes-castles](pages/sum-of-three-cubes-castles.md)] finds which values of `A^e(w, h)`, the number of castles of width `w ≥ 4` and height `h` with an even number of blocks, below `10^9` lie in it. Outside height 2 there are two, `A^e(6, 4) = 1729` and `A^e(4, 85) = 5^3 + 93^3`; at height 2 the closed form of `A^e(w, 2)` gives twice a cube, `2c^3`, at `w ≡ 5 (mod 12)` and a sum `c^3 + d^3` at `w ≡ 19 (mod 24)`
oeis_name: Numbers that are the sum of 2 positive cubes.

counts: the 3-smooth numbers `2^i 3^j`. It is not a castle count; it is a set of heights. A Mersenne castle ([[mersenne-castles](pages/mersenne-castles.md)]) is a castle whose neighboring columns have heights in the ratio of a perfect consonance, 1, 2, 3/2 or 4/3 or the inverse, and the heights that chains of such steps join to height 1 are the 3-smooth heights `2^i 3^j`, the class of height 1 under this consonance rule
oeis_name: 3-smooth numbers: numbers of the form 2^i*3^j with i, j >= 0.

counts: the positions, counted from 0, of the 1s of the infinite Fibonacci word (the limit of the substitution `0 → 01`, `1 → 0`), `1, 4, 6, 9, …`, the Wythoff compound sequence `⌊nφ²⌋ − 1` with `φ` the golden ratio. It is not a castle count; raising the columns at the 1s of a prefix of the word gives a Fibonacci-word castle, a castle of height 2 with no two neighboring columns of height 2 whose second row is a factor of the Fibonacci word, and these positions are its height-2 columns counted from 0. Counted from 1 they are the upper Wythoff numbers A001950 ([[fibonacci-castles-sub-families](pages/fibonacci-castles-sub-families.md)])
oeis_name: The Wythoff compound sequence AA: a(n) = floor(n*phi^2) - 1, where phi = (1+sqrt(5))/2.

counts: the infinite Fibonacci word `0, 1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 1, …`, the limit of the substitution `0 → 01`, `1 → 0` started from `0`. It is not a count. It has no two adjacent 1s, so every prefix is a Fibonacci tower: removing the bottom row of a Fibonacci castle (a castle of height 2 with no two neighboring columns of height 2) leaves a string of 0s and 1s with a 1 at each column of height 2, and every prefix of the word is such a string ([[fibonacci-castle](pages/fibonacci-castle.md)])
oeis_name: The infinite Fibonacci word (start with 0, apply 0->01, 1->0, take limit).

counts: the number of domino tilings of the `2n × 2n` square. It is not a castle count; [[castle-bdd-zdd](pages/castle-bdd-zdd.md)] quotes `A004003(4)`, the domino tilings of the `8 × 8` square, from Knuth's TAOCP section 7.1.4 as an example of the size of a family that a ZDD (zero-suppressed binary decision diagram, a compressed graph that stores a family of sets) can hold, a scale for storing the castles that way
oeis_name: Number of domino tilings (or dimer coverings) of a 2n X 2n square.

counts: the sequence `a(n) = 5a(n−1) − a(n−2)`, `0, 1, 5, 24, 115, …`. It is not a castle count; it is the second factor of a sandpile count. In the sink model of [[sandpile-group](pages/sandpile-group.md)] sand leaves the castle through one sink cell, and the sandpile group has order the number of spanning trees of the castle's graph. For the castle `(3, …, 3)` of height 3 and width `w` that order is `|K_sink| = |K_tide((2, …, 2))| · A004254(w) = F(2w) · A004254(w)`, where `F(2w)`, an even-indexed Fibonacci number, is the order of the group of the castle `(2, …, 2)` in the tide model, in which sand leaves through the bottom row (Dhar-Ruelle-Sen-Verma Appendix A, [[dhar-ruelle-sen-verma-1995-algebraic-aspects](pages/dhar-ruelle-sen-verma-1995-algebraic-aspects.md)], [[sandpile-census](pages/sandpile-census.md)])

the number of convex polyominoes of perimeter `2n`, polyominoes whose every row and every column is one unbroken run of cells, with Delest and Viennot's formula `p_{2n+8} = (2n + 11)4^n − 4(2n + 1)C(2n, n)` ([[algebraic-languages-and-polyominoes-enumeration](pages/algebraic-languages-and-polyominoes-enumeration.md)]). It is not a castle count; the castles among the convex polyominoes are the convex castles, whose skyline rises weakly and then falls weakly, and these are the stack polyominoes ([[convex-castle](pages/convex-castle.md)])
oeis_name: Number of convex polygons of perimeter 2n on square lattice.

counts: the number of balanced binary words of length `n` (the finite Sturmian words), words in which any two factors of the same length contain numbers of 1s that differ by at most one; OEIS gives `a(n) = 1 + Σ_{i=1}^{n} (n − i + 1)φ(i)` with `φ` Euler's totient. Half of it counts castles: the balanced castles of width `w`, the Fibonacci castles (castles of height 2 with no two neighboring columns of height 2) whose second row is a balanced word, number `A005598(w)/2 = A049703(w)` ([[fibonacci-castles-sub-families](pages/fibonacci-castles-sub-families.md)])

the number of castles of width 4 and height `h`, `A(4, h) = h^4 − (h−1)^4`: the skylines with every column between 1 and `h`, minus those that never reach `h`; the values at `h = 7` and `h = 9` are the Carmichael numbers 1105 and 2465 ([[hardy-ramanujan-castle](pages/hardy-ramanujan-castle.md)])
oeis_name: Rhombic dodecahedral numbers: n^4 - (n-1)^4.

counts: the bronze metallic sequence `0, 1, 3, 10, 33, 109, …`, `a(n) = 3a(n−1) + a(n−2)`, whose growth is the bronze mean `δ_3 = (3 + √13)/2` ([[metallic-means](pages/metallic-means.md)]). It is not itself a castle count. It enters through the ridge rule at height 4 (neighboring columns differ unless both have height 4): the ridge strips of height 4 and width `w` number `A006190(w + 1) + A006190(w)`, which is A003688(w + 1), and the ridge castles of height 4 grow by width like `δ_3^w` ([[metallic-strip-realizability](pages/metallic-strip-realizability.md)], [[proper-castle-projection](pages/proper-castle-projection.md)])

the trace sequence `2, 3, 11, 36, …`, `a(n) = 3a(n−1) + a(n−2)` with `a(0) = 2`, `a(1) = 3`, equal to `δ_3^n + δ̂_3^n` for the bronze mean `δ_3 = (3 + √13)/2` and its conjugate `δ̂_3` ([[metallic-means](pages/metallic-means.md)], [[castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk](pages/castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk.md)]). It is not a castle count; the bronze mean is the growth by width of the ridge castles of height 4, whose neighboring columns differ in height unless both have height 4 ([[proper-castle-projection](pages/proper-castle-projection.md)])

the number of parallelogram polyominoes of `n` cells, polyominoes whose column bottoms and column tops both rise weakly from left to right; one of the nine polyomino families counted by number of cells in the table on [[convex-polyomino-by-area](pages/convex-polyomino-by-area.md)], whose generating function is a ratio of q-Bessel series. It is not a castle count; the castles that are parallelogram polyominoes are the castles with a weakly increasing skyline ([[castle-add-a-column-equation](pages/castle-add-a-column-equation.md)])
oeis_name: Number of parallelogram polyominoes with n cells (also called staircase polyominoes, although that term is overused).

counts: the number of castles of height exactly 5 and area `n`, the number of cells, `A006979(n)`: reading the column heights in order makes a castle of area `n` a composition of `n`, and height 5 makes 5 its largest part, which is the OEIS definition ([[castles-of-height-h-by-area](pages/castles-of-height-h-by-area.md)])
oeis_name: a(n) is the number of compositions of n in which the maximum part size is 5.

counts: the number of castles of height exactly 6 and area `n`, the number of cells, `A006980(n)`: reading the column heights in order makes a castle of area `n` a composition of `n` with largest part 6, which the OEIS lists as the sixth column of the triangle A048004 ([[castles-of-height-h-by-area](pages/castles-of-height-h-by-area.md)])
oeis_name: Compositions: 6th column of A048004.

counts: Pascal's triangle of binomial coefficients `C(n, k)`. It is not a castle count; it is the toolkit behind every castle count given by binomial coefficients, such as the `C(2h + w − 3, w − 1)` convex castles of width `w` and height `h` (castles whose skyline rises weakly and then falls weakly, [[convex-castle](pages/convex-castle.md)]) and the castles of width `w` and height 2 with an even number of blocks, `A^e(w, 2) = Σ_j C(w + 1, 4j + 2)` ([[aocp-binomial-coefficients](pages/aocp-binomial-coefficients.md)])
oeis_name: Pascal's triangle read by rows: C(n,k) = binomial(n,k) = n!/(k!*(n-k)!), 0 <= k <= n.

counts: the reversion of the generating function of the Fibonacci numbers. It is not itself a castle count; up to sign it is the signed count of the Motzkin-path castles, the castles whose neighboring columns differ in height by at most 1 and whose two end columns have height 1 ([[motzkin-castles](pages/motzkin-castles.md)]): the number of those of width `w` with an even number of blocks minus the number with an odd number is `−A343773(w − 1)`, and `A343773(n) = (−1)^n A007440(n + 1)`
oeis_name: Reversion of g.f. for Fibonacci numbers 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, ....

counts: the number of self-avoiding rook paths joining opposite corners of an `n × n` grid. It is not a castle count; [[castle-bdd-zdd](pages/castle-bdd-zdd.md)] quotes `A007764(8)`, the corner-to-corner paths on the `8 × 8` grid of points, from Knuth's TAOCP section 7.1.4 as an example of the size of a family that a ZDD (zero-suppressed binary decision diagram, a compressed graph that stores a family of sets) can hold, a scale for storing the castles that way
oeis_name: Number of nonintersecting (or self-avoiding) rook paths joining opposite corners of an n X n grid.

counts: Knuth's ruler function `ρ(k)`, the exponent of the highest power of 2 dividing `k` (the 2-adic valuation), `0, 1, 0, 2, 0, 1, 0, 3, …` from `k = 1`. It is not a castle count; in Gray-code generation (TAOCP section 7.2.1.1) step `k` flips bit `ρ(k)`, the method behind listing castles one changed column at a time ([[aocp-generating-permutations-tuples](pages/aocp-generating-permutations-tuples.md)], [[castle-gray-code](pages/castle-gray-code.md)])
oeis_name: Exponent of highest power of 2 dividing n, a.k.a. the binary carry sequence, the ruler sequence, or the 2-adic valuation of n.

counts: the triangle of Stirling numbers of the second kind `{n k}`, the number of ways to split `n` elements into `k` nonempty subsets. It is not a castle count; it is part of Knuth's binomial-coefficient toolkit, converting between powers and falling factorials ([[aocp-binomial-coefficients](pages/aocp-binomial-coefficients.md)]), and Bender's four partition counts of a multiset reduce to it when no element repeats ([[bender-1974-partitions-of-multisets](pages/bender-1974-partitions-of-multisets.md)])
oeis_name: Triangle of Stirling numbers of the second kind, S2(n,k), n >= 1, 1 <= k <= n.

counts: the Mahonian numbers `T(n, k)`, the number of permutations of `{1, …, n}` with `k` inversions. Row `h` counts castles: a rainbow castle of height `h` has width `h` and a skyline that is a permutation of `{1, …, h}`, so the `h!` rainbow castles of height `h` whose skyline has `k` inversions (pairs of columns with the taller one on the left) number `T(h, k)` ([[aocp-combinatorics](pages/aocp-combinatorics.md)], [[castle-classification-shape](pages/castle-classification-shape.md)])
oeis_name: Triangle of Mahonian numbers T(n,k): coefficients in expansion of Product_{i=0..n-1} (1 + x + ... + x^i), where k ranges from 0 to A000217(n-1). Also enumerates permutations by their major index.

counts: the period-6 sequence `1, 1, 0, −1, −1, 0, …`, the coefficients of `1/(1 − x + x²)`, the inverse of the 6th cyclotomic polynomial. It is not a count; it appears in two signed counts. For the towers (castles minus their bottom row) of height at most 4 on a base of length `L` whose last column has odd height, the number with an even number of blocks minus the number with an odd number is `P_odd(4, L) = −2^L A010892(L − 1)` for `L ≥ 1` ([[tower-parity-sectors](pages/tower-parity-sectors.md)]). For the Euler castles (castles whose columns fall by 0 or 1 at each step and end at height 1) of semi-perimeter `s`, half the length of the boundary, the even-block minus the odd-block count is `−A010892(s − 2)` ([[euler-castles](pages/euler-castles.md)])
oeis_name: Inverse of 6th cyclotomic polynomial. A period 6 sequence.

counts: the number of hereditarily finite sets of rank at most `n`, `a(n + 1) = 2^{a(n)}` with `a(−1) = 0`: `0, 1, 2, 4, 16, 65536, …`. It is not a castle count; it marks the heights of the Ackermann castles of [[von-neumann-castles](pages/von-neumann-castles.md)]. The castle of a set is a bottom block carrying the castles of its members, and `ack(m)` is the castle of the set whose Ackermann code is `m`; it has height `h` exactly when `A014221(h − 2) ≤ m < A014221(h − 1)`, and width 1 exactly when `m` is a term, the code of one of the sets `∅`, `{∅}`, `{{∅}}`, …

the Catalan transform of the Jacobsthal numbers, `Σ_{j ≤ (n−1)/2} C(2n − 2j − 2, n − 1)`, a pair in Table 1 of Barry's paper on transforms of sequences by Riordan arrays ([[barry-2005-catalan-transform](pages/barry-2005-catalan-transform.md)]); OEIS names it the number of nodes of odd outdegree in all ordered rooted trees with `n` edges. It is not a castle count; it appears only as an entry of that table, and the castle reading on that page uses a different transform of the same paper
oeis_name: Number of nodes of odd outdegree in all ordered rooted (planar) trees with n edges.

counts: the even Lucas numbers `L(3n)`, `2, 4, 18, 76, …`, the trace `δ_4^n + δ̂_4^n` of the metallic mean `δ_4 = 2 + √5 = φ³` and its conjugate ([[metallic-means](pages/metallic-means.md)], [[castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk](pages/castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk.md)]). It is not a castle count; `δ_4` is the growth by width of the ridge castles of height 5, whose neighboring columns differ in height unless both have height 5 ([[proper-castle-projection](pages/proper-castle-projection.md)])
oeis_name: Even Lucas numbers: a(n) = L(3*n).

counts: the odd triangular numbers `1, 3, 15, 21, 45, …`. It is not a castle count; its partial sums A352116 measure a signed tower count. Write `P(k, L)` for the number of towers (castles minus their bottom row) of height at most `k` on a base of length `L` with an even number of blocks minus the number with an odd number; then `|P(k, 4)| = A352116(k + 1)`, the sum of the first `k + 1` odd triangular numbers ([[signed-tower-k-direction](pages/signed-tower-k-direction.md)], [[closed-form-hunting](pages/closed-form-hunting.md)])
oeis_name: Odd triangular numbers.

counts: the sequence with generating function `(1 − 4x)/(1 − 5x − x²)`, `1, 1, 6, 31, 161, …`, which shifted by one counts ridge strips of height 6: the skylines `(c_1, …, c_w)` with every `c_i` in `{1, …, 6}` in which neighboring columns differ in height unless both have height 6 number `A015449(w + 1)` ([[ridge-castle](pages/ridge-castle.md)], [[proper-castle-projection](pages/proper-castle-projection.md)]). A strip need not reach height 6, so this is the ridge castles of height 6 plus the `5 · 4^{w−1}` skylines on `{1, …, 5}` with no two neighboring columns of equal height; both grow by width like `δ_5 = (5 + √29)/2`
oeis_name: Expansion of (1-4*x)/(1-5*x-x^2).

counts: the number of palindromic castles of area `n`, the number of cells, `2^{⌊n/2⌋}`: reading the column heights in order makes a castle of area `n` a composition of `n`, and the castles equal to their mirror image are the symmetric compositions. With the `2^{n−1}` castles of area `n` they give the castles up to mirror image, `(2^{n−1} + 2^{⌊n/2⌋})/2` of them ([[castle-graph](pages/castle-graph.md)])
oeis_name: a(n) = 2^floor(n/2).

counts: the number of mountains of spheres on a `3 × ℓ` base, stacks in which every sphere above the base rests on four spheres below (Thomas and May). It is not a castle count. A mountain is a sequence of `ℓ` fountains, each leaning on the one before, and a fountain of width 3 is a brick-wall castle of width 3, a castle on bricks laid in running bond with each brick resting on two below; so this counts the sequences of `ℓ` such castles allowed by the leaning rule, a transfer-matrix count on the five fountains of width 3 ([[thomas-may-2022-mountain-counting](pages/thomas-may-2022-mountain-counting.md)], [[brick-wall-castles](pages/brick-wall-castles.md)])

Bender's `v((0, n))`, the number of partitions of the multiset in which each of `n` elements appears twice, with two equal parts allowed and no element repeated inside a part; OEIS lists it as the multigraphs on `n` labeled edges without loops. It is not a castle count, and Bender's blocks are the parts of a partition, unrelated to castle blocks. The wiki sets it beside the castles glued at height-1 columns from a given multiset of prime castles ([[prime-castles](pages/prime-castles.md)]), which correspond to the orderings of the multiset and are counted by a multinomial coefficient, where Bender counts unordered groupings ([[bender-1974-partitions-of-multisets](pages/bender-1974-partitions-of-multisets.md)])
oeis_name: Number of multigraphs on n labeled edges (without loops).

counts: Bender's `v*((0, n))`, the number of partitions of the multiset in which each of `n` elements appears twice, with two equal parts allowed and an element allowed twice inside a part (all partitions of that multiset); OEIS lists it as the multigraphs on `n` labeled edges with loops. It is not a castle count, and Bender's blocks are the parts of a partition, unrelated to castle blocks. The wiki sets it beside the castles glued at height-1 columns from a given multiset of prime castles ([[prime-castles](pages/prime-castles.md)]), which correspond to the orderings of the multiset and are counted by a multinomial coefficient, where Bender counts unordered groupings ([[bender-1974-partitions-of-multisets](pages/bender-1974-partitions-of-multisets.md)])
oeis_name: Number of multigraphs on n labeled edges (with loops). Also number of genetically distinct states amongst n individuals.

counts: the number of Motzkin paths of `n` steps with no `UD`, `UU` or `DD` (up then down, two ups, two downs), which Deutsch and Elizalde (§4.2) match with the strictly alternating bargraphs `U^{i_1} H D^{k_1} H U^{i_2} H D^{k_2} H ⋯ U^{i_m} H D^{k_m}` by semi-perimeter, sending semi-perimeter `s` (up steps plus columns) to paths of `s − 3` steps. A bargraph is a castle read as its boundary path, so these bargraphs are the castles of odd width whose columns alternately fall and rise, `c_1 > c_2 < c_3 > ⋯ < c_w`, the sign-alternating castles that fall first of [[castle-classification-shape](pages/castle-classification-shape.md)], leaving out the single cell `(1)` ([[deutsch-elizalde-2016-bargraphs-cornerless-motzkin](pages/deutsch-elizalde-2016-bargraphs-cornerless-motzkin.md)])
oeis_name: Number of Dyck n-paths with ascents and descents of length equal to 1 (mod 3).

counts: the Ballot transform of the Fibonacci numbers, `0, 1, 4, 16, 65, 267, …`, a pair in Table 2 of Barry's paper on transforms of sequences by Riordan arrays ([[barry-2005-catalan-transform](pages/barry-2005-catalan-transform.md)]). It is not a castle count; it appears only as an entry of that table

the triangle of trinomial coefficients, row `n` the coefficients of `(1 + x + x^2)^n`: the number of words of length `n` in the steps `U` (up one), `R` (level) and `D` (down one) by final height, with no floor or ceiling. It is not a castle count; it is the unconstrained count from which the castle grammar ([[generalized-dyck-grammar](pages/generalized-dyck-grammar.md)]) keeps only the words that stay within the castle's height ([[urd-step-strings](pages/urd-step-strings.md)]), and the method of images writes the 1-smooth strips between heights 1 and `h` (skylines whose neighboring columns differ by at most 1) as alternating sums of these coefficients ([[1-smooth-castles](pages/1-smooth-castles.md)])
oeis_name: Triangle of trinomial coefficients T(n,k) (n >= 0, 0 <= k <= 2*n), read by rows: n-th row is obtained by expanding (1 + x + x^2)^n.

counts: `n(n + 3)`, `0, 4, 10, 18, 28, …`. It is not itself a castle count; minus 2 it counts open-stroke castles, the castles whose graph, with one ground vertex joined to every bottom cell, has exactly two vertices of odd degree, so that one stroke from one of them to the other crosses every side between two cells and every side on the ground once. Summed over all odd widths, the open-stroke castles of height `h` number `h² + 3h − 2 = A028552(h) − 2 = 2·A034856(h)`, in five families ([[konigsberg-castles](pages/konigsberg-castles.md)])

`F(3n + 1)`, `1, 3, 13, 55, …`, the differences `p_n − q_n` of the numerators and denominators of the continued-fraction convergents of the metallic mean `δ_4 = 2 + √5 = φ³`, which are the numerators of the convergents of `δ_4 − 1` ([[castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk](pages/castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk.md)]). It is not a castle count; `δ_4` is the growth by width of the ridge castles of height 5, whose neighboring columns differ in height unless both have height 5 ([[proper-castle-projection](pages/proper-castle-projection.md)])
oeis_name: a(n) = Fibonacci(3*n + 1).

counts: the number of polyominoes whose bounding box is exactly 2 by `n` (inscribed in the rectangle: inside it and touching all four sides), `I(2, n) = Q_{n+1} − 2` with `Q` the Pell-Lucas numbers A001333. It is not a castle count; it bounds one. A castle of width 2 and height `n` is such a polyomino, since its full bottom row touches the bottom and both sides and its tallest column touches the top, so `A(2, n) = 2n − 1 ≤ I(2, n)` ([[inscribed-polyomino](pages/inscribed-polyomino.md)], [[marin-2024-polyominoes-in-rectangle](pages/marin-2024-polyominoes-in-rectangle.md)])
oeis_name: Number of not-necessarily-symmetric n X 2 crossword puzzle grids.

counts: the number of polyominoes whose bounding box is exactly 3 by `n` (inscribed in the rectangle: inside it and touching all four sides), growing like `5.0566^n`. It is not a castle count; it bounds one. A castle of width 3 and height `n` is such a polyomino, since its full bottom row touches the bottom and both sides and its tallest column touches the top, so `A(3, n) = n^3 − (n − 1)^3 ≤ I(3, n)`; at `n = 3` there are 19 castles among 111 such polyominoes ([[inscribed-polyomino](pages/inscribed-polyomino.md)], [[marin-2024-polyominoes-in-rectangle](pages/marin-2024-polyominoes-in-rectangle.md)])
oeis_name: Not necessarily symmetric n X 3 crossword puzzle grids.

counts: the number of polyominoes whose bounding box is exactly 4 by `n` (inscribed in the rectangle: inside it and touching all four sides). It is not a castle count; it bounds one. A castle of width 4 and height `n` is such a polyomino, since its full bottom row touches the bottom and both sides and its tallest column touches the top, so `A(4, n) = n^4 − (n − 1)^4 ≤ I(4, n)` ([[inscribed-polyomino](pages/inscribed-polyomino.md)], [[marin-2024-polyominoes-in-rectangle](pages/marin-2024-polyominoes-in-rectangle.md)])
oeis_name: Not necessarily symmetric n X 4 crossword puzzle grids.

counts: the Ackermann codes of the von Neumann ordinals, `0, 1, 3, 11, 2059, …`, with `a(n + 1) = a(n) + 2^{a(n)}`. It is not a count; it indexes castles. The castle of a set is a bottom block carrying the castles of its members left to right, one empty column between neighbors, and the von Neumann castle `vN(n)`, the castle of the ordinal `n = {0, 1, …, n − 1}`, is `ack(A034797(n))`, the castle of the set whose Ackermann code is `A034797(n)` ([[von-neumann-castles](pages/von-neumann-castles.md)])

the triangle `T(n, k) = C(n, 2k)`, every other entry of each row of Pascal's triangle. It counts towers by blocks: a tower of height at most 1 on a base of length `w` (a castle of height at most 2 with its bottom row removed) is a string of 0s and 1s, and those with `b` blocks, runs of 1s, number `C(w + 1, 2b) = T(w + 1, b)`. Putting the bottom row back adds one block, which gives the binomial identities `A^e(w, 2) = Σ_j C(w + 1, 4j + 2)` and `A^o(w, 2) = Σ_{j ≥ 1} C(w + 1, 4j)` for the castles of width `w` and height 2 with an even and an odd number of blocks ([[oeis-mining-pe502](pages/oeis-mining-pe502.md)])
oeis_name: Triangular array formed by taking every other term of each row of Pascal's triangle.

counts: the triangle of multinomial coefficients `n!/(k_1! ⋯ k_m!)`, one for each partition of `n` in Abramowitz-Stegun order, the numbers of permutations of a multiset (Knuth Vol. 1 §1.2.6 and Vol. 3 §5.1.2). It is not a castle count; a castle's step string, a word in `U` (up one row), `R` (one column) and `D` (down one row), is a permutation of a multiset of letters, and the words with given numbers of each letter number `C(n; #U, #R, #D)` ([[aocp-multinomial-coefficients](pages/aocp-multinomial-coefficients.md)], [[aocp-multisets](pages/aocp-multisets.md)])
oeis_name: Triangle T(n,k) read by rows: multinomial coefficients for the partitions of n listed in Abramowitz-Stegun order, 1 <= k <= A000041(n).

counts: the sum of every fourth entry of row `n` of Pascal's triangle, starting at `C(n, 1)`: `Σ_j C(n, 4j + 1)`, the residue-1 member of the order-4 hyperbolic family [[hyperbolic-sequence-family](pages/hyperbolic-sequence-family.md)]. It is not a castle count; it appears beside its siblings `A038505` and `A038503`, which count the castles of height 2 with an even and with an odd number of blocks (a block being a maximal run of cells in one row): `A^e(w, 2) = A038505(w + 1)` and `A^o(w, 2) = A038503(w + 1) − 1`
oeis_name: Sum of every 4th entry of row n in Pascal's triangle, starting at "n choose 1".

counts: the triangle of ballot numbers `(2k + 1)/(n + k + 1) · C(2n, n + k)`, the matrix of Barry's generalized Ballot transform `Cat ∘ Bin`, the Catalan transform composed with the binomial transform [[barry-2005-catalan-transform](pages/barry-2005-catalan-transform.md)]. It is not a castle count; it appears in the summary of Barry's paper, whose companion transform (aerate, then take the binomial transform) counts the 1-smooth strips, skylines whose neighboring columns differ in height by at most 1, with both end columns pinned
oeis_name: Triangle formed from even-numbered columns of triangle of expansions of powers of x in terms of Chebyshev polynomials U_n(x).

counts: the numerators of the convergents to `√8`, the fractions obtained by cutting off its continued fraction `[2; 1, 4, 1, 4, …]` (period 2) after each term; the denominators are `A041011`. It is not a castle count. It sits in the crosswalk table of [[castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk](pages/castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk.md)] because `√8 = 2δ_2 − 2`, where `δ_2 = (2 + √8)/2 = 1 + √2`, the silver mean, is the metallic mean of order 2, `(a + √(a² + 4))/2` at `a = 2`, and the growth rate by width of the ridge castles of height 3 (castles whose neighboring columns differ in height unless both have height 3, [[ridge-castle](pages/ridge-castle.md)])
oeis_name: Numerators of continued fraction convergents to sqrt(8).

counts: the denominators of the convergents to `√8`, the fractions obtained by cutting off its continued fraction `[2; 1, 4, 1, 4, …]` (period 2) after each term; the numerators are `A041010`. It is not a castle count. It sits in the crosswalk table of [[castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk](pages/castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk.md)] because `√8 = 2δ_2 − 2`, where `δ_2 = (2 + √8)/2 = 1 + √2`, the silver mean, is the metallic mean of order 2, `(a + √(a² + 4))/2` at `a = 2`, and the growth rate by width of the ridge castles of height 3 (castles whose neighboring columns differ in height unless both have height 3, [[ridge-castle](pages/ridge-castle.md)])
oeis_name: Denominators of continued fraction convergents to sqrt(8).

counts: the numerators of the convergents to `√13`, the fractions obtained by cutting off its continued fraction `[3; 1, 1, 1, 1, 6, …]` (period 5) after each term; the denominators are `A041019`. It is not a castle count. It sits in the crosswalk table of [[castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk](pages/castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk.md)] because `√13 = 2δ_3 − 3`, where `δ_3 = (3 + √13)/2`, the bronze mean, is the metallic mean of order 3, `(a + √(a² + 4))/2` at `a = 3`, and the growth rate by width of the ridge castles of height 4 (castles whose neighboring columns differ in height unless both have height 4, [[ridge-castle](pages/ridge-castle.md)])
oeis_name: Numerators of continued fraction convergents to sqrt(13).

counts: the denominators of the convergents to `√13`, the fractions obtained by cutting off its continued fraction `[3; 1, 1, 1, 1, 6, …]` (period 5) after each term; the numerators are `A041018`. It is not a castle count. It sits in the crosswalk table of [[castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk](pages/castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk.md)] because `√13 = 2δ_3 − 3`, where `δ_3 = (3 + √13)/2`, the bronze mean, is the metallic mean of order 3, `(a + √(a² + 4))/2` at `a = 3`, and the growth rate by width of the ridge castles of height 4 (castles whose neighboring columns differ in height unless both have height 4, [[ridge-castle](pages/ridge-castle.md)])
oeis_name: Denominators of continued fraction convergents to sqrt(13).

counts: the numerators of the convergents to `√20`, the fractions obtained by cutting off its continued fraction `[4; 2, 8, 2, 8, …]` (period 2) after each term; the denominators are `A041031`. It is not a castle count. It sits in the crosswalk table of [[castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk](pages/castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk.md)] because `√20 = 2δ_4 − 4`, where `δ_4 = (4 + √20)/2 = 2 + √5 = φ³` is the metallic mean of order 4, `(a + √(a² + 4))/2` at `a = 4`, and the growth rate by width of the ridge castles of height 5 (castles whose neighboring columns differ in height unless both have height 5, [[ridge-castle](pages/ridge-castle.md)])
oeis_name: Numerators of continued fraction convergents to sqrt(20).

counts: the denominators of the convergents to `√20`, the fractions obtained by cutting off its continued fraction `[4; 2, 8, 2, 8, …]` (period 2) after each term; the numerators are `A041030`. It is not a castle count. It sits in the crosswalk table of [[castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk](pages/castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk.md)] because `√20 = 2δ_4 − 4`, where `δ_4 = (4 + √20)/2 = 2 + √5 = φ³` is the metallic mean of order 4, `(a + √(a² + 4))/2` at `a = 4`, and the growth rate by width of the ridge castles of height 5 (castles whose neighboring columns differ in height unless both have height 5, [[ridge-castle](pages/ridge-castle.md)])
oeis_name: Denominators of continued fraction convergents to sqrt(20).

counts: the numerators of the convergents to `√29`, the fractions obtained by cutting off its continued fraction `[5; 2, 1, 1, 2, 10, …]` (period 5) after each term; the denominators are `A041047`. It is not a castle count. It sits in the crosswalk table of [[castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk](pages/castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk.md)] because `√29 = 2δ_5 − 5`, where `δ_5 = (5 + √29)/2` is the metallic mean of order 5, `(a + √(a² + 4))/2` at `a = 5`, and the growth rate by width of the ridge castles of height 6 (castles whose neighboring columns differ in height unless both have height 6, [[ridge-castle](pages/ridge-castle.md)])
oeis_name: Numerators of continued fraction convergents to sqrt(29).

counts: the denominators of the convergents to `√29`, the fractions obtained by cutting off its continued fraction `[5; 2, 1, 1, 2, 10, …]` (period 5) after each term; the numerators are `A041046`. It is not a castle count. It sits in the crosswalk table of [[castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk](pages/castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk.md)] because `√29 = 2δ_5 − 5`, where `δ_5 = (5 + √29)/2` is the metallic mean of order 5, `(a + √(a² + 4))/2` at `a = 5`, and the growth rate by width of the ridge castles of height 6 (castles whose neighboring columns differ in height unless both have height 6, [[ridge-castle](pages/ridge-castle.md)])
oeis_name: Denominators of continued fraction convergents to sqrt(29).

counts: the number of 1s in all compositions of `n + 1`, which the wiki reads as a count of castle columns. A castle of area `n` (its number of cells) is a composition of `n` into its column heights, and the columns of height `j` over all castles of area `n` total `A045623(n − j)`, which is `(n − j + 3) 2^{n−j−2}` for `j < n`, from Balado and Silvestre's count of runs in binary strings [[balado-silvestre-2026-runs-binary-strings](pages/balado-silvestre-2026-runs-binary-strings.md)]. At `j = 1` this is the total number of height-1 columns, `A045623(n − 1)`; since a castle with `k` height-1 columns has `k + 1` prime factors (the pieces left by cutting it at its height-1 columns, [[prime-castles](pages/prime-castles.md)]), a castle of area `n ≥ 2` has `(n + 6)/4` prime factors on average
oeis_name: Number of 1's in all compositions of n+1.

counts: the denominators of `C(2n, n)/4^n`. It is not a castle count. On [[fractional-block-count](pages/fractional-block-count.md)] they are the denominators of the Grunwald-Letnikov weights of order 1/2, the weights of a fractional difference of the skyline whose positive parts sum to the area at order 0 and to the block count at order 1. On [[fractional-width-and-height](pages/fractional-width-and-height.md)] they are the denominators of the weights `1, 1/2, 3/8, 5/16, …` (the coefficients of `(1 − x)^{−1/2}`) of the square root of the strip rule of the chain order, the rule that lets a column be followed by any column at least as high; a square root `R` with `R² = M` is a half-column rule, two steps of which make one step of `M`
oeis_name: a(n) = denominator of binomial(2n,n)/4^n.

counts: a triangle: `T(n, k)` is the number of binary strings of length `n` whose longest run of 1s has length exactly `k`. Through castles it counts the castles of area `n` (number of cells) and height `h`: writing each column of height `c` as a run of `c − 1` 1s, with a single 0 between neighboring columns, turns them into the binary strings of length `n − 1` whose longest run of 1s has length `h − 1`, so they number `T(n − 1, h − 1)` [[castles-of-height-h-by-area](pages/castles-of-height-h-by-area.md)]; the heights 3 to 6 are the columns `A000100`, `A000102`, `A006979` and `A006980`
oeis_name: Triangular array read by rows: T(n,k) = number of binary vectors of length n whose longest run of consecutive 1's has length k, for n >= 0, 0 <= k <= n.

counts: Hickerson's auxiliary count `b(n)`: the number of horizontally convex polyominoes of `n` cells (every row one unbroken run of cells) whose top row has exactly one cell, equal to `3a(n−1) − 4a(n−2)` for `n ≥ 4`. It is not a castle count; Hickerson uses the four counts `b`, `c`, `d`, `e` to prove that all horizontally convex polyominoes of `n` cells, `a(n)`, satisfy `a(n) = 5a(n−1) − 7a(n−2) + 4a(n−3)` for `n ≥ 5` [[counting-horizontally-convex-polyominoes](pages/counting-horizontally-convex-polyominoes.md)]. A quarter turn makes horizontally convex polyominoes the column-convex ones, which contain every castle [[horizontally-convex-polyomino](pages/horizontally-convex-polyomino.md)]
oeis_name: Number of horizontally convex n-ominoes in which the top row has exactly 1 square.

counts: Hickerson's auxiliary count `c(n)`: the number of horizontally convex polyominoes of `n` cells (every row one unbroken run of cells) whose top row has at least two cells, the rightmost of them directly above the leftmost cell of the second row, equal to `a(n) − 4a(n−1) + 4a(n−2)` for `n ≥ 4`. It is not a castle count; Hickerson uses the four counts `b`, `c`, `d`, `e` to prove that all horizontally convex polyominoes of `n` cells, `a(n)`, satisfy `a(n) = 5a(n−1) − 7a(n−2) + 4a(n−3)` for `n ≥ 5` [[counting-horizontally-convex-polyominoes](pages/counting-horizontally-convex-polyominoes.md)]. A quarter turn makes horizontally convex polyominoes the column-convex ones, which contain every castle [[horizontally-convex-polyomino](pages/horizontally-convex-polyomino.md)]
oeis_name: Number of horizontally convex n-ominoes in which the top row has at least 2 squares and the rightmost square in the top row is above the leftmost square in the second row.

counts: Hickerson's auxiliary count `d(n)`: the number of horizontally convex polyominoes of `n` cells (every row one unbroken run of cells) whose top row has exactly one cell, not above the rightmost cell of the second row, equal to `2a(n−1) − 4a(n−2)` for `n ≥ 4`. It is not a castle count; Hickerson uses the four counts `b`, `c`, `d`, `e` to prove that all horizontally convex polyominoes of `n` cells, `a(n)`, satisfy `a(n) = 5a(n−1) − 7a(n−2) + 4a(n−3)` for `n ≥ 5` [[counting-horizontally-convex-polyominoes](pages/counting-horizontally-convex-polyominoes.md)]. A quarter turn makes horizontally convex polyominoes the column-convex ones, which contain every castle [[horizontally-convex-polyomino](pages/horizontally-convex-polyomino.md)]
oeis_name: Number of horizontally convex n-ominoes in which the top row has exactly 1 square, which is not above the rightmost square in the second row.

counts: Hickerson's auxiliary count `e(n)`: the number of horizontally convex polyominoes of `n` cells (every row one unbroken run of cells) whose top row has exactly one cell, not above the rightmost cell of the second row, and whose second row has its rightmost cell above the leftmost cell of the third row, equal to `a(n) − 3a(n−1)` for `n ≥ 3`. It is not a castle count; Hickerson uses the four counts `b`, `c`, `d`, `e` to prove that all horizontally convex polyominoes of `n` cells, `a(n)`, satisfy `a(n) = 5a(n−1) − 7a(n−2) + 4a(n−3)` for `n ≥ 5` [[counting-horizontally-convex-polyominoes](pages/counting-horizontally-convex-polyominoes.md)]. A quarter turn makes horizontally convex polyominoes the column-convex ones, which contain every castle [[horizontally-convex-polyomino](pages/horizontally-convex-polyomino.md)]
