oeis_name: Number of horizontally convex n-ominoes in which the top row has exactly 1 square, which is not above the rightmost square in the second row and the rightmost square in the second row is above the leftmost square in the third row.

counts: the coefficients of the continued fraction `[0; x, x², x³, …]` (in the OEIS, the coefficient of `x^{−n}`). It is not a castle count; up to sign it is a signed polyomino count. In a parallelogram polyomino (one bounded by two up-right lattice paths that meet only at their ends) every row is one unbroken run of cells, so its rows are its blocks, and the number of parallelogram polyominoes of `n` cells with an even number of rows minus the number with an odd number of rows is `−A049346(n)`, from the continued fraction `−q/(1 + q³/(1 + q⁵/(1 + ⋯)))` [[convex-polyomino-by-area](pages/convex-polyomino-by-area.md)]
oeis_name: Coefficient of x^(-n) in expansion of continued fraction 0, x, x^2, x^3, x^4, ... .

counts: the numbers that are both `x^3 + y^3` and `z^3 + 1` with `1 < x < y < z`, the Fermat near misses for cubes, in increasing order. It is not a castle count. Its first term is `1729 = 9^3 + 10^3 = 12^3 + 1`, which is a castle count, `A^e(6, 4)`, the number of castles of width 6 and height 4 with an even number of blocks; and `9^3 + 10^3 = 12^3 + 1` is the row `n = −1` of Ramanujan's near-miss family `a_n^3 + b_n^3 = c_n^3 + (−1)^n`, reached by running its recurrence backward [[hardy-ramanujan-castle](pages/hardy-ramanujan-castle.md)]
oeis_name: Diophantine equation x^3 + y^3 = z^3 + 1 with 1 < x < y < z ("Fermat near misses").

counts: Ramanujan's a-series `a_n`, the first of three sequences with `a_n^3 + b_n^3 = c_n^3 + (−1)^n` for every `n ≥ 0`, a family of near misses to `x^3 + y^3 = z^3`. It is not a castle count; [[hardy-ramanujan-castle](pages/hardy-ramanujan-castle.md)] reaches it from the castle count `A^e(6, 4) = 1729`. Its terms grow by the factor `δ_9^2 = (83 + 9√85)/2`, the square of the ninth metallic mean `δ_9 = (9 + √85)/2`, which is the largest eigenvalue of the ridge rule at height 10, the strip rule on the heights 1 to 10 that lets neighboring columns have equal height only at the top height 10 [[ridge-castle](pages/ridge-castle.md)]
oeis_name: Ramanujan's a-series: expansion of (1+53x+9x^2)/(1-82x-82x^2+x^3).

counts: Ramanujan's b-series `b_n` in the near-miss family `a_n^3 + b_n^3 = c_n^3 + (−1)^n`; the three series have the same denominator `(1 + x)(1 − 83x + x^2)` in their generating functions, so they satisfy the same recurrence. It is not a castle count; it belongs to the family that [[hardy-ramanujan-castle](pages/hardy-ramanujan-castle.md)] reaches from the castle count `A^e(6, 4) = 1729`
oeis_name: Ramanujan's b-series: expansion of (2-26x-12x^2)/(1-82x-82x^2+x^3).

counts: Ramanujan's c-series `c_n` in the near-miss family `a_n^3 + b_n^3 = c_n^3 + (−1)^n`. It is not a castle count; it belongs to the family that [[hardy-ramanujan-castle](pages/hardy-ramanujan-castle.md)] reaches from the castle count `A^e(6, 4) = 1729`. The Berlekamp-Massey algorithm, which finds the shortest linear recurrence fitting a run of terms [[berlekamp-massey](pages/berlekamp-massey.md)], recovers the order-3 recurrence `s_n = 82s_{n−1} + 82s_{n−2} − s_{n−3}` from `c_0, …, c_5`, and the same from `c_0, …, c_11`
oeis_name: Ramanujan's c-series: expansion of (2+8x-10x^2)/(1-82x-82x^2+x^3).

counts: the number of strongly connected tournaments on `n` vertices (a tournament has exactly one directed edge between any two vertices, and it is strong when every vertex can reach every other). It is not a castle count. On [[tree-castle-by-area](pages/tree-castle-by-area.md)] it is the column beside Tetali's four basic tournaments, the strong tournaments that are unique (every tournament with the same score vector, the list of out-degrees, is isomorphic to it): 1 of 1 at `n = 3`, 1 of 1 at `n = 4`, 1 of 6 at `n = 5`, and 0 of 35 and 0 of 353 at `n = 6, 7`. The unique tournaments on `n` vertices are built from those four, and they are as many as the tree skylines (no two neighboring columns of height at least 2) of height at most 4 and area `n − 1`
oeis_name: Number of strongly connected tournaments on n nodes.

counts: the metallic sequence of order 5, `x_n = 5x_{n−1} + x_{n−2}` with `x_0 = 0`, `x_1 = 1`, listed from `x_1`, so that `A052918(n) = x_{n+1}`; one step apart, its terms are the numerators and denominators of the convergents of `δ_5 = (5 + √29)/2 = [5; 5, 5, …]` [[castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk](pages/castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk.md)]. It is not a castle count; `δ_5` is the largest eigenvalue of the ridge rule at height 6, so the ridge castles of height 6 (castles whose neighboring columns differ in height unless both have height 6, [[ridge-castle](pages/ridge-castle.md)]) grow like `δ_5^w` by width

the numerators of the convergents of `δ_3 − 1`, where `δ_3 = (3 + √13)/2 = [3; 3, 3, …]` is the bronze mean: `p_n − q_n` for the convergents `p_n/q_n` of `δ_3`, with generating function `(1 − x)/(1 − 3x − x²)` [[castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk](pages/castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk.md)]. It is not a castle count; the bronze mean is the growth rate by width of the ridge castles of height 4, castles whose neighboring columns differ in height unless both have height 4 [[ridge-castle](pages/ridge-castle.md)]
oeis_name: Expansion of g.f.: (1-x)/(1 - 3*x - x^2).

counts: the expansion of `2x(1 − x)/(1 − 3x + x²)`, which is `2F_{2n−1}` for `n > 0`, `F` the Fibonacci numbers. It is not itself a castle count; shifted by one it counts the Hilbert strips of height 4, the skylines `(c_1, …, c_w)` with every `c_i` in `{1, …, 4}` in which no two neighboring columns differ in height by exactly 1: the formula of `A126358` writes them as `A052995(w + 1) = 2F_{2w+1}` [[hilbert-castles](pages/hilbert-castles.md)]. A strip need not reach height 4; the Hilbert castles of height 4, which do, number `2F_{2w+1} − 2^w − 1`
oeis_name: Expansion of 2*x*(1 - x)/(1 - 3*x + x^2).

counts: the decimal digits of the plastic number `ψ = 1.3247…`, the real root of `x^3 = x + 1` [[plastic-number](pages/plastic-number.md)]. It is not a count. On castles it is a growth rate: the maximal castles (Fibonacci castles in which no further column can be raised to height 2) grow like `ψ^w` by width [[fibonacci-castles-sub-families](pages/fibonacci-castles-sub-families.md)], and the ridge castles of height 2 grow like `ψ^A` by area `A`, the number of cells [[ridge-castle](pages/ridge-castle.md)]
oeis_name: Decimal expansion of real root of x^3 - x - 1 (the plastic constant).

counts: the integers not congruent to 4 or 5 modulo 9 (`0, 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 8, …`). Every sum of three integer cubes is in this list, and under Heath-Brown's conjecture these are exactly the sums of three cubes [[sums-of-three-cubes](pages/sums-of-three-cubes.md)]. It is not a castle count; it enters through the question of which castle counts are sums of three cubes. `A^e(w, h)`, the number of castles of width `w` and height `h` with an even number of blocks, is periodic modulo 9 in the width and in the height, so under that conjecture each count is decided by its residue [[sum-of-three-cubes-castles](pages/sum-of-three-cubes-castles.md)]
oeis_name: Numbers that are not congruent to 4 or 5 mod 9.

counts: the number of tricoverings of an `n`-set, Bender's `c((0, 0, n))`: the partitions of the multiset in which each of `n` elements appears three times into blocks with no two blocks equal and no element repeated inside a block [[multiset-partitions](pages/multiset-partitions.md)], [[bender-1974-partitions-of-multisets](pages/bender-1974-partitions-of-multisets.md)]. It is not a castle count; Bender's blocks are the parts of a partition, unrelated to the blocks of a castle
oeis_name: Tricoverings of an n-set.

counts: the number of fixed convex polyominoes of `n` cells, polyominoes in which every row and every column is one unbroken run of cells, counted up to translation; one of the nine polyomino families counted by number of cells in the table on [[convex-polyomino-by-area](pages/convex-polyomino-by-area.md)]. It is not a castle count: a convex polyomino need not stand on a full bottom row, and the castles among them are the stack polyominoes, the convex castles. Its entry gives the prefactor `2.9195985097…` of the asymptotic count `c · μ^n`, with `μ = 2.3091385933…` the Klarner-Rivest constant
oeis_name: Number of fixed convex polyominoes with n cells.

counts: the number of fixed directed convex polyominoes of `n` cells, counted up to translation: convex polyominoes (every row and every column one unbroken run of cells) whose column bottoms rise weakly from left to right and whose column tops rise and then fall; one of the nine polyomino families counted by number of cells in the table on [[convex-polyomino-by-area](pages/convex-polyomino-by-area.md)]. It is not a castle count; the castles sit in that table as the bar graphs, `2^{n−1}` of them
oeis_name: Number of fixed directed convex polyominoes with n cells.

counts: the number of runs of 1s in the binary expansion of `n`. It is not a castle count. In Marin's automaton for the polyominoes inscribed in a `w × h` rectangle (with a cell on every side of it), `n` is the occupancy of one row read as a binary number, its runs are the row's pieces, and the Catalan number `C_m` with `m = A069010(n)` counts the noncrossing ways to group them into connected components in the formula for the number of states [[marin-2024-polyominoes-in-rectangle](pages/marin-2024-polyominoes-in-rectangle.md)]; the castles are the inscribed polyominoes that are bar graphs
oeis_name: Number of runs of 1's in the binary representation of n.

counts: the number of heights `2^i 3^j ≤ h`, the 3-smooth numbers up to `h`. It is not a castle count. For the Mersenne castles (castles whose neighboring columns have heights in ratio 1, 2, 3/2 or 4/3 or the inverse, the perfect consonances, [[mersenne-castles](pages/mersenne-castles.md)]) it is the size of the largest class of heights in `{1, …, h}` that chains of consonant steps connect, the class of the height 1, and it grows like `(ln h)²/(2 ln 2 ln 3)`
oeis_name: Number of 3-smooth numbers <= n.

counts: the triangle `T(n, k) = C(n + k, 2k)`, known in the Fibonacci literature as the DFF triangle; it is the absolute value of the matrix of Barry's inverse generalized Ballot transform [[barry-2005-catalan-transform](pages/barry-2005-catalan-transform.md)]. It is not a castle count; it appears in the summary of Barry's paper beside `A039599`, the matrix of the Ballot transform
oeis_name: Triangle read by rows: T(n, k) = binomial(n + k, 2*k).

counts: the number of `n × n` 0/1 matrices whose eigenvalues are all real and nonnegative. It is not a castle count; read on the wiki, it counts strip rules, the `h × h` 0/1 matrices that say which column heights may stand next to which [[castle-strip](pages/castle-strip.md)]: 13, 261 and 15418 of them at heights 2, 3, 4 have all eigenvalues real and nonnegative. Those with no eigenvalue 0 have a real square root, the question being whether a rule `M` is two steps `R² = M` of a half-column rule `R` [[fractional-width-and-height](pages/fractional-width-and-height.md)]
oeis_name: Number of n X n real (0,1)-matrices with all eigenvalues >= 0.

counts: the trace sequence of the metallic mean `δ_5 = (5 + √29)/2`: `y_n = δ_5^n + δ̂_5^n`, with `δ̂_5 = 5 − δ_5` its conjugate, so that `y_0 = 2`, `y_1 = 5` and `y_n = 5y_{n−1} + y_{n−2}`, the trace of the convergent matrix of `δ_5` [[metallic-means](pages/metallic-means.md)], [[castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk](pages/castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk.md)]. It is not a castle count; `δ_5` is the growth rate by width of the ridge castles of height 6, castles whose neighboring columns differ in height unless both have height 6 [[ridge-castle](pages/ridge-castle.md)]

the number of triangle stacks of large Schröder type with `n` triangles, counted by area alone. These are Bala's stacks of triangles on a bottom row of contiguous down triangles, each stack the area under a large Schröder path [[bala-2019-triangle-stacks-large-schroder-type](pages/bala-2019-triangle-stacks-large-schroder-type.md)]. They are close to castles: a stack on `k` down triangles is a keystone castle of width `k + 1` (a castle on the triangular tiling, [[keystone-castles](pages/keystone-castles.md)]) with its bottom row of up triangles removed
oeis_name: Expansion of continued fraction A(x) = 1/(1-x-x^2/(1-x^3-x^4/(1-x^5-x^6/(1-x^7-x^8/(1-...))))).

counts: the number of triangle stacks of large Schröder type with `n` down triangles in all and any number of up triangles, the row sums of Bala's array of these stacks by down and up triangles. The stacks stand on a bottom row of contiguous down triangles, each stack the area under a large Schröder path [[bala-2019-triangle-stacks-large-schroder-type](pages/bala-2019-triangle-stacks-large-schroder-type.md)]. A stack on `k` down triangles is a keystone castle of width `k + 1` (a castle on the triangular tiling, [[keystone-castles](pages/keystone-castles.md)]) with its bottom row of up triangles removed
oeis_name: Expansion of continued fraction A(x) = 1/(1-x-x/(1-x^2-x^2/(1-x^3-x^3/(1-x^4-x^4/(1-...))))).

counts: the number of peakless Motzkin meanders of length `n`: paths of `n` steps, up `U`, down `D` and level `H`, that never go below their starting height, may end at any height, and never take an up step directly followed by a down step (`UD`, a peak); Prodinger (2025) prints this row as "valleyless" [[prodinger-2025-cornerless-motzkin-bargraphs](pages/prodinger-2025-cornerless-motzkin-bargraphs.md)]. It is not a castle count; it relaxes the tower words, which spell the towers of a castle (the castle minus its bottom row) with no `UD` (a block of width 0), no `DU` (two touching blocks) and a return to height 0 [[tower-word-language](pages/tower-word-language.md)]: these meanders keep the ban on `UD` and drop the other two rules
oeis_name: Number of left factors of peakless Motzkin paths of length n.

counts: the decimal digits of the supergolden ratio `1.4655712…`, the real root of `x^3 = x^2 + 1`, also called Narayana's cows constant. It is not a count; it is the growth rate by area of the tree castles of height 2, which are the Fibonacci castles (castles of height 2 with no two neighboring columns of height 2): those with `n` cells number `A000930(n + 1) − 1` [[q-fibonacci-castle](pages/q-fibonacci-castle.md)], [[tree-castle-by-area](pages/tree-castle-by-area.md)]
oeis_name: Decimal expansion of (2/3)*cos( (1/3)*arccos(29/2) ) + 1/3, the real root of x^3 - x^2 - 1.

counts: the number of (≤2)-covers of an `n`-set, Bender's `c*((0, n))`: the partitions of the multiset in which each of `n` elements appears twice into blocks with no two blocks equal, an element allowed to repeat inside a block [[multiset-partitions](pages/multiset-partitions.md)], [[bender-1974-partitions-of-multisets](pages/bender-1974-partitions-of-multisets.md)]. It is not a castle count; Bender's blocks are the parts of a partition, unrelated to the blocks of a castle
oeis_name: Number of (<=2)-covers of an n-set.

counts: the number of regular tournaments on `2n + 1` vertices up to isomorphism, those in which every vertex has out-degree `n`: 1, 1, 3 at 3, 5, 7 vertices. It is not a castle count. In Tetali's proof the regular score vectors `(1, 1, 1)` and `(2, 2, 2, 2, 2)` each have one realizing tournament, while `(3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3)` has three, so it is not unique [[forcibly-simple-score-vector](pages/forcibly-simple-score-vector.md)]; through that proof the unique tournaments are counted like the tree skylines of height at most 4 by area [[tree-castle-by-area](pages/tree-castle-by-area.md)]
oeis_name: Number of unlabeled regular tournaments with 2n+1 nodes.

counts: a triangle read by rows: row `n` lists the coefficients of `G(x)^n`, with `G` the generating function of `A100234`, and its row sums are `6^n − 1` for `n > 0`. It is not a castle count; it appears only because its secondary diagonal, divided by the row number, is `A100237`, the numerators of the convergents of `δ_5 − 1` in the crosswalk table of [[castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk](pages/castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk.md)]
oeis_name: Triangle, read by rows, of the coefficients of [x^k] in G100234(x)^n such that the row sums are 6^n-1 for n>0, where G100234(x) is the g.f. of A100234.

counts: the numerators of the convergents of `δ_5 − 1`, where `δ_5 = (5 + √29)/2 = [5; 5, 5, …]`: `p_n − q_n` for the convergents `p_n/q_n` of `δ_5`, with generating function `(1 − x)/(1 − 5x − x²)` (`1, 4, 21, 109, 566, …`) [[castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk](pages/castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk.md)]; the OEIS defines it as the secondary diagonal of the triangle `A100235` divided by the row number. It is not a castle count; `δ_5` is the growth rate by width of the ridge castles of height 6 [[ridge-castle](pages/ridge-castle.md)]
oeis_name: Secondary diagonal of triangle A100235 divided by row number: a(n) = A100235(n+1,n)/(n+1) for n >= 0.

counts: a triangle: `T(n, k)` is the number of compositions of `n` with exactly `k` parts equal to 1. Every castle of area `n` (number of cells) is a composition of `n` into its column heights, so `T(n, k)` counts the castles of area `n` with `k` columns of height 1, and these have `k + 1` prime factors, the pieces left by cutting a castle at its height-1 columns [[prime-castles](pages/prime-castles.md)]; shifted by one in `k`, the triangle counts the castles of area `n` by their number of prime factors
oeis_name: Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) is the number of compositions of n having exactly k parts equal to 1.

counts: the number of Dyck paths of semilength `n` that avoid the pattern `UUDU`, which by the bijection `µ` of Baril, Flórez and Ramírez equals the number of Dyck paths of semilength `n` with no peak at a height divisible by 3 ([[baril-florez-ramirez-2026-generalized-narayana-arrays](pages/baril-florez-ramirez-2026-generalized-narayana-arrays.md)]). It is not a castle count; it appears as the residue-class-0 companion of A082582, which counts both the castles of semi-perimeter `n` and the Dyck paths with no peak at a height `≡ 2 (mod 3)`
oeis_name: Row sums of triangle A105632.

counts: the Lucas and Lehmer numbers with parameters `(1 ± √−7)/2`, the Lucas sequence `U_L(1, 2)` of the roots of `x² − x + 2`. It is not a castle count. Its negative is `P_odd(2, L)`, the signed count of the towers of height at most 2 on a base of length `L` whose last column has odd height, where a tower is a castle with its bottom row removed and each tower counts +1 or −1 by the parity of its number of blocks ([[tower-parity-sectors](pages/tower-parity-sectors.md)]). So the signed tower count is `P(2, L) = 2^L − A107920(L)`, and the even-block castles of height 3 number `A^e(w, 3) = (3^w − 2^{w+1} + A146559(w+1) + A107920(w))/2` ([[castle-fibers-char-2-walkthrough](pages/castle-fibers-char-2-walkthrough.md)], [[new-sequence-fw3](pages/new-sequence-fw3.md)])
oeis_name: Lucas and Lehmer numbers with parameters (1 +- sqrt(-7))/2.

counts: the coefficients of `1/η_12`, the reciprocal of the degree-6 polynomial `1 − 7x + 15x² − 6x³ − 11x⁴ + 6x⁵ + x⁶`. It is not a castle count. The anchored 1-smooth castles of height 6 (castles whose neighboring columns differ in height by at most 1 and whose first column has height 1) have width generating function `x^6/(η_12 + x^6)`, so they agree with A122611 for six terms, widths 6 to 11, and differ at width 12, 6038 castles against 6039 ([[1-smooth-castles](pages/1-smooth-castles.md)])

the unsigned Stirling numbers of the first kind `[n k]`, the permutations of `n` elements with `k` cycles. It is not a castle count. Its column `[n 1] = (n − 1)!` counts the cyclic orders of `n` labeled points, the count that [[castles-as-upgraded-cycle-count](pages/castles-as-upgraded-cycle-count.md)] starts from and pairs with constructions on castles ([[aocp-binomial-coefficients](pages/aocp-binomial-coefficients.md)])
oeis_name: Triangle of unsigned Stirling numbers of the first kind (see A048994), read by rows, T(n,k) for 0 <= k <= n.

counts: the number of possible column states for self-avoiding polygons in a slit of width `n`, a state count of a transfer automaton. It is not a castle count. Marin cites it beside the row states of the automaton for polyominoes inscribed in a rectangle (A378947) as a related state count ([[marin-2024-polyominoes-in-rectangle](pages/marin-2024-polyominoes-in-rectangle.md)])
oeis_name: Number of possible column states for self-avoiding polygons in a slit of width n.

counts: the integers congruent to 4 or 5 modulo 9, which are never sums of three cubes. It is not a castle count. [[sum-of-three-cubes-castles](pages/sum-of-three-cubes-castles.md)] asks which castle counts fall in it: the even-block castles of width `w` and height 2, `A^e(w, 2)`, do exactly when `w ≡ 9 (mod 12)`, the even-block castles of width 3 and height `h`, `A^e(3, h)`, exactly when `h ≡ 4, 6 (mod 18)`, and the castle counts `A(3m, h)` of width a multiple of 3, each a difference of two cubes, never ([[sums-of-three-cubes](pages/sums-of-three-cubes.md)])
oeis_name: Numbers that are congruent to 4 or 5 mod 9.

counts: Bender's count `v((0, 0, n))`: the number of partitions of the multiset in which each of `n` distinct elements appears three times, into blocks in which no element repeats, with repeated blocks allowed (`1, 1, 4, 39, 862`). It is not a castle count; Bender's blocks are the parts of a partition, unrelated to castle blocks. The wiki sets these counts beside the castles built from a given multiset of prime castles, which are ordered and counted by a multinomial coefficient, while Bender's groupings are unordered ([[multiset-partitions](pages/multiset-partitions.md)], [[bender-1974-partitions-of-multisets](pages/bender-1974-partitions-of-multisets.md)])
oeis_name: Number of tri-coverings of a set.

counts: the number of words of length `n` over the letters `{0, 1, 2}` in which every nonzero letter is at most one of its neighbors (no nonzero letter is a strict local maximum, with a virtual 0 beyond each end), Hardin's words `W_2(n)`. It is not itself a castle count. By the Hardin word identity it is a signed tower count, `W_2(L + 1) = P_even(10, L)/2^L`, where `P_even(10, L)` is the number of towers (castles with their bottom row removed) of height at most 10 on a base of length `L` whose last column has even height, each counted +1 or −1 by the parity of its number of blocks ([[hardin-word-identity](pages/hardin-word-identity.md)]). It also counts the skylines of width `n − 1` with every column of height 1 to 3 and tower spacing at least 2, meaning every run of empty cells in a row between two filled cells has length at least 2; these need not reach height 3, so they are the castles of every height up to 3 with that spacing ([[tower-spacing-castles](pages/tower-spacing-castles.md)])
oeis_name: Number of n X 1 0..2 arrays with every nonzero element less than or equal to some horizontal or vertical neighbor.

counts: the number of words of length `n` over the letters `{0, 1, …, 5}` in which every nonzero letter is at most one of its neighbors (no nonzero letter is a strict local maximum, with a virtual 0 beyond each end), Hardin's words `W_5(n)`. It is not itself a castle count. By the Hardin word identity it is a signed tower count, `W_5(L + 1) = P_even(22, L)/2^L`, where `P_even(22, L)` is the number of towers (castles with their bottom row removed) of height at most 22 on a base of length `L` whose last column has even height, each counted +1 or −1 by the parity of its number of blocks ([[hardin-word-identity](pages/hardin-word-identity.md)]). It also counts the skylines of width `n − 1` with every column of height 1 to 6 and tower spacing at least 2, meaning every run of empty cells in a row between two filled cells has length at least 2; these need not reach height 6, so they are the castles of every height up to 6 with that spacing ([[tower-spacing-castles](pages/tower-spacing-castles.md)])
oeis_name: Number of nX1 0..5 arrays with every nonzero element less than or equal to some horizontal or vertical neighbor.

counts: the number of words of length `n` over the letters `{0, 1, 2, 3}` in which every nonzero letter is at most one of its neighbors (no nonzero letter is a strict local maximum, with a virtual 0 beyond each end), Hardin's words `W_3(n)`. It is not itself a castle count. By the Hardin word identity it is a signed tower count, `W_3(L + 1) = P_even(14, L)/2^L`, where `P_even(14, L)` is the number of towers (castles with their bottom row removed) of height at most 14 on a base of length `L` whose last column has even height, each counted +1 or −1 by the parity of its number of blocks ([[hardin-word-identity](pages/hardin-word-identity.md)]). It also counts the skylines of width `n − 1` with every column of height 1 to 4 and tower spacing at least 2, meaning every run of empty cells in a row between two filled cells has length at least 2; these need not reach height 4, so they are the castles of every height up to 4 with that spacing ([[tower-spacing-castles](pages/tower-spacing-castles.md)])
oeis_name: Number of nX1 0..3 arrays with every nonzero element less than or equal to some horizontal or vertical neighbor.

counts: the number of words of length `n` over the letters `{0, 1, …, 4}` in which every nonzero letter is at most one of its neighbors (no nonzero letter is a strict local maximum, with a virtual 0 beyond each end), Hardin's words `W_4(n)`. It is not itself a castle count. By the Hardin word identity it is a signed tower count, `W_4(L + 1) = P_even(18, L)/2^L`, where `P_even(18, L)` is the number of towers (castles with their bottom row removed) of height at most 18 on a base of length `L` whose last column has even height, each counted +1 or −1 by the parity of its number of blocks ([[hardin-word-identity](pages/hardin-word-identity.md)]). It also counts the skylines of width `n − 1` with every column of height 1 to 5 and tower spacing at least 2, meaning every run of empty cells in a row between two filled cells has length at least 2; these need not reach height 5, so they are the castles of every height up to 5 with that spacing ([[tower-spacing-castles](pages/tower-spacing-castles.md)])
oeis_name: Number of n X 1 0..4 arrays with every nonzero element less than or equal to some horizontal or vertical neighbor.

counts: the number of castles of height exactly 4 in which every column has height 1 or 4, counted by semi-perimeter `s`, the width plus the number of blocks, half the length of the boundary: `A209231(s − 1)`. Deleting the bottom row and lengthening each run of height-4 columns by 3 turns these castles into the binary words of length `s − 1`, not all zero, whose runs of 1s are all at least 4 long, which A209231 counts with the roles of 0 and 1 exchanged ([[balado-silvestre-2026-runs-binary-strings](pages/balado-silvestre-2026-runs-binary-strings.md)], [[golden-silver-bronze-plastic-castles](pages/golden-silver-bronze-plastic-castles.md)])
oeis_name: Number of binary words of length n such that there is at least one 0  and every run of consecutive 0's is of length >= 4.

counts: the number of skylines of width `w` with every column of height 1 or 2 and tower spacing at least 7 (in every row, each run of empty cells between two filled cells has length at least 7), `spacing_7(w, 2) = A217838(w)`. A skyline need not reach height 2, so this is the castles of height 2 with that spacing plus the flat row `(1, …, 1)`. It is Hardin's count of the 0/1 arrays of length `w` that are minima of 7 adjacent elements of a longer 0/1 array, column 7 of A217839 ([[tower-spacing-castles](pages/tower-spacing-castles.md)], [[balado-silvestre-2026-runs-binary-strings](pages/balado-silvestre-2026-runs-binary-strings.md)])
oeis_name: Number of n element 0..1 arrays with each element the minimum of 7 adjacent elements of a random 0..1 array of n+6 elements.

counts: Hardin's table of the 0/1 arrays of length `w` that are minima of `g` adjacent elements of a longer 0/1 array, which is the whole height-2 row of the tower-spacing table: `T(w, g) = spacing_g(w, 2)`, the number of skylines of width `w` with every column of height 1 or 2 and tower spacing at least `g` (in every row, each run of empty cells between two filled cells has length at least `g`). A skyline need not reach height 2, so each entry is the castles of height 2 with that spacing plus the flat row `(1, …, 1)` ([[tower-spacing-castles](pages/tower-spacing-castles.md)])
oeis_name: T(n,k)=Number of n element 0..1 arrays with each element the minimum of k adjacent elements of a random 0..1 array of n+k-1 elements.

counts: Hardin's table of the arrays over `{0, 1, 2}` of length `w` that are minima of `g` adjacent elements of a longer such array, which is the height-3 row of the tower-spacing table: `T(w, g) = spacing_g(w, 3)`, the number of skylines of width `w` with every column of height 1 to 3 and tower spacing at least `g` (in every row, each run of empty cells between two filled cells has length at least `g`). A skyline need not reach height 3, so each entry counts the castles of every height up to 3 with that spacing ([[tower-spacing-castles](pages/tower-spacing-castles.md)])
oeis_name: T(n,k) = number of n-element 0..2 arrays with each element the minimum of k adjacent elements of a random 0..2 array of n+k-1 elements.

counts: Hardin's table of the arrays over `{0, 1, 2, 3}` of length `w` that are minima of `g` adjacent elements of a longer such array, which is the height-4 row of the tower-spacing table: `T(w, g) = spacing_g(w, 4)`, the number of skylines of width `w` with every column of height 1 to 4 and tower spacing at least `g` (in every row, each run of empty cells between two filled cells has length at least `g`). A skyline need not reach height 4, so each entry counts the castles of every height up to 4 with that spacing ([[tower-spacing-castles](pages/tower-spacing-castles.md)])
oeis_name: T(n,k) = number of n-element 0..3 arrays with each element the minimum of k adjacent elements of a random 0..3 array of n+k-1 elements.

counts: the number of triangle stacks of `n` triangles: the decompositions of the area beneath a small Schröder path into unit up and down triangles, whose bottom row is a run of contiguous up triangles (Paul Tek's sequence, with Bala's continued fraction). A stack is a row of keystone castles side by side, a keystone castle being a castle on the triangular tiling with a full bottom row and no overhang, so this counts sequences of keystone castles by number of cells ([[bala-2019-area-beneath-small-schroder-paths](pages/bala-2019-area-beneath-small-schroder-paths.md)], [[keystone-castles](pages/keystone-castles.md)])
oeis_name: Number of stacks of n triangles, pointing upwards or downwards depending on row parity.

counts: the positions of the positive integers in the ordering of the rational numbers generated from 1 by `x → x + 1` and `x → −1/x`. It is not a castle count. It agrees with `A003410(n)` for `n = 4..35`, and for widths `w ≥ 4` `A003410(w)` is the number of `(1, 3)`-RLL castles of width `w`: Fibonacci castles (castles of height 2 with no two neighboring columns of height 2) whose second row has runs of 0s at least 1 long between 1s and at most 3 long everywhere. Colin Barker's conjectured generating function for A226136 is their generating function ([[fibonacci-castles-sub-families](pages/fibonacci-castles-sub-families.md)], [[fibonacci-castle](pages/fibonacci-castle.md)])
oeis_name: Positions of the positive integers in the ordering of rational numbers as generated by the rules: 1 is in S, and if nonzero x is in S, then x+1 and -1/x are in S.

counts: the number of `n × n` 0/1 matrices that are the square of a 0/1 matrix. It is not a castle count. A strip rule of height `h` is an `h × h` 0/1 matrix saying which column height may follow which ([[castle-strip](pages/castle-strip.md)]), and the half-column problem on [[fractional-width-and-height](pages/fractional-width-and-height.md)] asks which rules are two steps of another 0/1 rule: 8, 88 and 3245 rules at heights 2, 3 and 4, the terms of A226321
oeis_name: Number of real {0,1} matrices n X n which are the square of a {0,1} matrix.

counts: the absolute value of the signed count of parallelogram polyominoes of area `n`, the number of cells: the number with even height minus the number with odd height is `(−1)^n A227310(n)`. A parallelogram polyomino is a polyomino whose column bottoms and column tops both weakly increase. These are polyominoes outside the castle family; on such row-convex shapes the castle block count equals the height, so height parity plays the role of the Project Euler 502 block parity. The signed count grows like `1.23729^n`, against `2.30914^n` for all parallelogram polyominoes ([[convex-polyomino-by-area](pages/convex-polyomino-by-area.md)])

the number of triangle stacks of Dyck type, the stacks of unit up and down triangles beneath a Dyck path (a small Schröder path with no flat step), by the number `k` of up triangles in the bottom row, which is the semilength of the path, and by the number of down triangles. Every triangle stack is a row of keystone castles side by side, keystone castles being castles on the triangular tiling with a full bottom row and no overhang ([[bala-2019-area-beneath-small-schroder-paths](pages/bala-2019-area-beneath-small-schroder-paths.md)], [[keystone-castles](pages/keystone-castles.md)])
oeis_name: Triangle defined by g.f. A(x,q) such that: A(x,q) = 1 + x*A(q*x,q)*A(x,q), as read by terms k=0..n*(n-1)/2 in rows n>=0.

counts: Hardin's table of the arrays of length `w` that are maxima of three adjacent elements of a longer array over `{0, …, k}`, which is the spacing-3 column of the tower-spacing table: `T(w, k) = spacing_3(w, k + 1)`, the number of skylines of width `w` with every column of height 1 to `k + 1` and tower spacing at least 3 (in every row, each run of empty cells between two filled cells has length at least 3). A skyline need not reach the top height, so each entry counts the castles of every height up to `k + 1` with that spacing ([[tower-spacing-castles](pages/tower-spacing-castles.md)])
oeis_name: Two-dimensional array read by antidiagonals: T(n,k) = number of arrays of maxima of three adjacent elements of some length n+2 0..k array.

counts: the iterated logarithm `log2*(n)`, version 3: the number of times `log_2` is applied to `n` until the result is at most 1. It is not a count. The Ackermann castle `ack(m)`, the castle of the hereditarily finite set whose code is `m`, has height `1 + A230864(m + 1)` ([[von-neumann-castles](pages/von-neumann-castles.md)])
oeis_name: log2*(n) (version 3): number of iterations log_2(log_2(log_2(...(n)...))) required for the result to be <= 1.

counts: the number of triangle stacks of Dyck type, the stacks of unit up and down triangles beneath a Dyck path (a small Schröder path with no flat step), by area `n`, the number of triangles, and by the number `k` of up triangles in the bottom row, which is the semilength of the path. Every triangle stack is a row of keystone castles side by side, keystone castles being castles on the triangular tiling with a full bottom row and no overhang ([[bala-2019-area-beneath-small-schroder-paths](pages/bala-2019-area-beneath-small-schroder-paths.md)], [[keystone-castles](pages/keystone-castles.md)])
oeis_name: Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) is the number of Dyck paths of semilength k such that the area between the x-axis and the path is n (n>=0; 0<=k<=n).

counts: the decimal digits of `β = 3.2055694304…`, the growth constant of Klarner and Rivest for the row-convex polyominoes (every row one unbroken strip of cells) counted by area, the largest root of `y³ − 5y² + 7y − 4`. It is not a count. Those polyominoes are A001169, and turned a quarter turn they are the column-convex polyominoes, which contain every castle ([[klarner-rivest-1974-convex-n-ominoes](pages/klarner-rivest-1974-convex-n-ominoes.md)], [[convex-polyomino-by-area](pages/convex-polyomino-by-area.md)])
oeis_name: Decimal expansion of 'v', an auxiliary constant associated with the asymptotic number of row-convex polyominoes.

counts: the number of bargraphs of semi-perimeter `n` whose first column has height `k`; bargraphs are castles, and the semi-perimeter is the width plus the number of blocks, half the length of the boundary. It is the first of the bargraph statistic sequences A273342 to A276068 of Deutsch and Elizalde ([[deutsch-elizalde-2016-bargraphs-cornerless-motzkin](pages/deutsch-elizalde-2016-bargraphs-cornerless-motzkin.md)], [[castle-perimeter](pages/castle-perimeter.md)])
oeis_name: Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) is the number of bargraphs of semiperimeter n having length of first column k (n>=2, k>=1).

counts: the total length of the first descents over all bargraphs of semi-perimeter `n`, a descent being a maximal run of consecutive down steps of the boundary; it sums a statistic over the castles of semi-perimeter `n` (bargraphs are castles, and the semi-perimeter is the width plus the number of blocks) and does not count them. It is the last of the bargraph statistic sequences A273342 to A276068 of Deutsch and Elizalde ([[deutsch-elizalde-2016-bargraphs-cornerless-motzkin](pages/deutsch-elizalde-2016-bargraphs-cornerless-motzkin.md)], [[castle-perimeter](pages/castle-perimeter.md)])
oeis_name: Sum of the lengths of the first descents in all bargraphs having semiperimeter n (n>=2). A descent is a maximal sequence of consecutive down steps.

counts: the decimal digits of `μ = 2.3091385933…`, the Klarner-Rivest constant, the common growth constant by area of the parallelogram, directed convex and convex polyominoes. It is not a count. The convex polyominoes contain the stack polyominoes, which are the convex castles, the castles whose skyline rises and then falls ([[convex-polyomino-by-area](pages/convex-polyomino-by-area.md)], [[bender-1974-convex-n-ominoes](pages/bender-1974-convex-n-ominoes.md)], [[convex-castle](pages/convex-castle.md)])
oeis_name: Decimal expansion of the Klarner-Rivest polyomino constant.

counts: the number of simple tournaments on `n` vertices up to isomorphism, `1, 1, 1, 0, 3, 15, 197, 4008` for `n ≤ 8`. A tournament has one directed edge between every two vertices, and it is simple when for every set `M` of at least two and fewer than all vertices some vertex outside `M` beats a vertex of `M` and is beaten by one ([[simple-tournament](pages/simple-tournament.md)]). It is not a castle count; simple tournaments are the tool of Tetali's classification of the unique tournaments, which [[tree-castle-by-area](pages/tree-castle-by-area.md)] matches with the tree skylines of height at most 4
oeis_name: Number of simple tournaments with n nodes.

counts: `I(w, h)`, the number of polyominoes inscribed in a `w × h` rectangle, that is, with a cell on each of its four sides, so that the bounding box is exactly `w × h`. It counts more than castles: every castle of width `w` and height `h` is one of these, the castles are the bargraphs among them, and `A(w, h) ≤ I(w, h)` ([[inscribed-polyomino](pages/inscribed-polyomino.md)])
oeis_name: Array read by antidiagonals: T(m,n) is the number of fixed polyominoes that have a width of m and height of n.

counts: the number of cornerless Motzkin meanders of length `n`: paths of up, down and flat steps that never go below the axis, may end at any height, and have no peak `UD` and no valley `DU`. They are the prefixes of tower words, the cornerless Motzkin paths that encode castles once their bottom row is removed, so a meander is a castle interrupted mid-build (Prodinger 2025, [[prodinger-2025-cornerless-motzkin-bargraphs](pages/prodinger-2025-cornerless-motzkin-bargraphs.md)], [[tower-word-continued-fraction](pages/tower-word-continued-fraction.md)])
oeis_name: Peak- and valleyless Motzkin meanders.

counts: Bender's count `c*((0, 0, n))`: the number of partitions of the multiset in which each of `n` distinct elements appears three times, into blocks that may repeat an element, with no two blocks equal (`1, 2, 17, 364, 14595`). It is not a castle count; Bender's blocks are the parts of a partition, unrelated to castle blocks. The wiki sets these counts beside the castles built from a given multiset of prime castles, which are ordered and counted by a multinomial coefficient, while Bender's groupings are unordered ([[multiset-partitions](pages/multiset-partitions.md)], [[bender-1974-partitions-of-multisets](pages/bender-1974-partitions-of-multisets.md)])
oeis_name: Number of nonnegative integer matrices with n columns and any number of nonzero distinct rows with every column summing to 3 up to permutation of rows.

counts: Bender's count `v*((0, 0, n))`: the number of all partitions of the multiset in which each of `n` distinct elements appears three times, repeated elements inside a block and repeated blocks both allowed (`1, 3, 31, 686, 27036`). It is not a castle count; Bender's blocks are the parts of a partition, unrelated to castle blocks. The wiki sets these counts beside the castles built from a given multiset of prime castles, which are ordered and counted by a multinomial coefficient, while Bender's groupings are unordered ([[multiset-partitions](pages/multiset-partitions.md)], [[bender-1974-partitions-of-multisets](pages/bender-1974-partitions-of-multisets.md)])
oeis_name: Number of (3*n) X n matrices with nonnegative integer entries and each column sum being 3 up to permutation of rows.

counts: the number of triangle stacks (the decompositions of the area beneath a small Schröder path into unit up and down triangles) by area `n`, the number of triangles, and by the number `k` of up triangles in the bottom row. Every triangle stack is a row of keystone castles side by side, keystone castles being castles on the triangular tiling with a full bottom row and no overhang ([[bala-2019-area-beneath-small-schroder-paths](pages/bala-2019-area-beneath-small-schroder-paths.md)], [[keystone-castles](pages/keystone-castles.md)])
oeis_name: Triangle read by rows: T(n,k) is the number of small Schröder paths of semilength k such that the area between the path and the x-axis is equal to n (n >= 0; 0 <= k <= n).

counts: the number of triangle stacks (the decompositions of the area beneath a small Schröder path into unit up and down triangles) by area `n`, the number of triangles, and by the number `k` of down triangles. Every triangle stack is a row of keystone castles side by side, keystone castles being castles on the triangular tiling with a full bottom row and no overhang ([[bala-2019-area-beneath-small-schroder-paths](pages/bala-2019-area-beneath-small-schroder-paths.md)], [[keystone-castles](pages/keystone-castles.md)])
oeis_name: Irregular triangle read by rows: T(n,k) is the number of small Schröder paths such that the area between the path and the x-axis is equal to n and contains k down-triangles.

counts: the number of subwords `UDDD` in the nondecreasing Dyck paths of length `2n`. It is not a castle count. It agrees with the anchored 1-smooth castles of height 4 (castles whose neighboring columns differ in height by at most 1 and whose first column has height 1) through width 10 only: at width 11 the castles number 5205 and the entry has 5206, an example of a short prefix that is not a match ([[oeis-cross-referencing](pages/oeis-cross-referencing.md)], [[1-smooth-castles](pages/1-smooth-castles.md)])
oeis_name: Number of subwords of the form UDDD in nondecreasing Dyck paths of length 2*n.

counts: the number of row states of Marin's automaton for the polyominoes with bounding box of width `n`, a count of automaton states. Read along the columns, a polyomino inscribed in a box of height `h` needs `A378947(h)` states, while a castle needs only the `h` states of the castle strip, one per column height, because every castle column stands on the full bottom row ([[marin-2024-polyominoes-in-rectangle](pages/marin-2024-polyominoes-in-rectangle.md)], [[inscribed-polyomino](pages/inscribed-polyomino.md)], [[castle-strip](pages/castle-strip.md)])
oeis_name: Number of row states in an automaton for the enumeration of the number of fixed polyominoes with bounding box of width n.

counts: the city-building sequence, in which `a(n)` is the lowest height `k` at which a new building sees exactly `k` of the buildings before it. It is not a count. For each width `w` its terms `a(2), …, a(w + 1)` form a city-building castle, a castle in which, with the ground in front as a column of height 0, every column sees exactly as many earlier columns as its height; these are the city-building castles built by always taking the lowest legal next column ([[city-building-castles](pages/city-building-castles.md)])
oeis_name: The city-building sequence: a(n) = the height h of the shortest building which can see exactly h earlier buildings.
